For R=S⁺ with (S,S⁺) a perfectoid Tate pair and S⁺ p-torsion-free (for instance R=O_C) this is the statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel, a node of a packet that is not yet in the atlas; the node keeps it as a hypothesis and consumers cite that node. For integral perfectoid rings not of this form no node states it (BMS1 §3.3, p. 27; Bhatt, Proposition 9.3(4)). The pinned Mathlib has the surjectivity of θ (WittVector.surjective_fontaineTheta) and no statement about its kernel.

gaps.title: Finite limits in the big crystalline site (Stacks Lemma 60.8.2)
gaps.detail: Stacks Lemma 60.8.2 (CRIS(X/S) has all finite nonempty limits and the forgetful functor commutes with them) has no proof in the source: 'Omitted. Hint: See Lemma 60.5.3 for the affine case.' Lemma 60.7.4 (fibre products of PD schemes), which the gluing uses, has only a sketch. The gluing of the affine construction has to be written out.

gaps.title: Exactness of i_! and the morphism π for non-affine X
gaps.detail: Stacks proves that i_! is exact, hence that π exists, only when X and S are affine: 'In the affine case this follows from Lemma 60.5.6. We omit the proof in general.' The small-site morphism f_cris=π_Y∘f_CRIS∘i_X depends on π_Y. Missing: a set of objects of Cris(X/S) covering the final object of (X/S)_CRIS for arbitrary X.

gaps.title: Composition of the morphisms of small crystalline topoi
gaps.detail: For the small topoi, (g∘f)_cris≅g_cris∘f_cris is not stated in Stacks (Remark 60.9.7 only records one square with the structure morphisms). Since g_cris∘f_cris=π_Z∘g_CRIS∘i_Y∘π_Y∘f_CRIS∘i_X and i_Y∘π_Y is not the identity, a proof is needed: every morphism from an object over X to an object of Cris(Z/S″) factors, locally, through an object of Cris(Y/S′).

gaps.title: Étale crystalline site and its comparison with the Zariski site
gaps.detail: The stage asks for the étale variant of the crystalline site and its comparison with the Zariski one. Stacks Definition 60.8.4 defines étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf coverings of thickenings but develops only the Zariski topology; no acquired source states or proves the comparison of the crystalline topoi or of the cohomology of quasi-coherent crystals for the two topologies. The stage asks for descent 'for the chosen topology'. The topology of this packet is the Zariski topology of the Stacks crystalline site (CR.1/crystalline-site). No source read for the packet (Stacks, Crystalline Cohomology; BMS1 §2; Ekedahl; the Berthelot–Ogus corrigendum) states étale descent for crystalline cohomology, and none is stated here. Invariance of the total complex under refinement of the cover and under change of the surjections P_λ→C_λ, which the roadmap's extension obligations ask for, is likewise not stated in the source.

gaps.title: Quasi-nilpotence in étale coordinates
gaps.detail: For a smooth A-algebra P′ with étale coordinates x_1,…,x_d, the direct coordinate condition on D′ (for every m and every i, θ_iᵏ(m)∈pM′ for k≫0) is not shown in Stacks to agree with the transported condition of Lemma 60.17.5; the footnote there says the condition 'is tricky to formulate for (M′,∇′) over D′'. The comparison needs D′(1)≅D′⟨ξ_1,…,ξ_d⟩^∧ for étale coordinates, which is in Berthelot–Ogus (Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, §§3–4), a source that was not acquired. Berthelot's definition of quasi-nilpotence (Cohomologie cristalline, LNM 407, II 4.3.5–4.3.6; Berthelot–Ogus §4) is in local étale coordinates x_1,…,x_d on Z_n: every local section is annihilated by a power of each ∇(∂/∂x_i). That this agrees with the condition used here (transport to the envelope of a polynomial algebra, Stacks Lemma 60.17.5) is not in the acquired sources; Esnault–Groechenig refer to Stacks tag 07JE for 'the precise definition'.

gaps.title: Verifications omitted in Stacks Proposition 60.17.4 and Lemma 60.17.5
gaps.detail: Stacks omits, in the proof of Proposition 60.17.4: that the restriction maps a^*F_T→F_T′ are independent of the choice of f, that the construction extends from affine objects to all of Cris(X/S), that it is a functor, and that it is quasi-inverse to the functor of Lemma 60.17.3; and, in the proof of Lemma 60.17.5, that c_{id,b∘a} is horizontal ('which we omit'). These five verifications have to be supplied.

gaps.title: Crystals and connections for a formally smooth lift (Stacks Remark 60.17.6)
gaps.detail: Formally smooth case: Stacks Remark 60.17.6 asserts the equivalence for a surjection P→C with P/A having the strong lifting property, with the comment 'Details will be added here if we ever need this'. The stage asks for a 'smooth/formally smooth lift'; no acquired source proves this case.

gaps.title: Crystals and connections on a non-affine scheme
gaps.detail: Global case: for X not affine with a closed embedding into a smooth S-scheme, or for a smooth formal lift, the equivalence between crystals and modules with integrable quasi-nilpotent connection on the PD envelope (with quasi-nilpotence expressed in local coordinates) is not in Stacks. The sources are Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (LNM 407), II 4.3.10 and IV 1.6.5, as quoted by Esnault–Groechenig §2.6, and Berthelot–Ogus §§4 and 6; none was acquired.

gaps.title: Crystalline cohomology as a derived limit over the reductions modulo p^e (Stacks Remark 60.24.10)
gaps.detail: Stacks Remark 60.24.10, RΓ(Cris(X/S),F)=Rlim_eRΓ(Cris(X/S_e),F_e), belongs to §60.24, whose results are stated without proof ('In this section we mention some results whose proof is missing'). The hint (reduce to injective F; restriction to Cris(X/S_e) preserves injectives; surjectivity of Γ(F_{e+1})→Γ(F_e); Γ(F)=lim_eΓ(F_e)) has to be written out.

gaps.title: Linearization along an embedding into a smooth scheme
gaps.detail: The stage asks for the linearization functor for a closed embedding of X into a smooth S-scheme and for its acyclicity. Not covered by the statements above and not in the Stacks chapter: (a) for P smooth over S but not an affine space, the local identification of D_T with a PD polynomial algebra over O_T, which needs étale-local invariance of PD envelopes; (b) the global statements Ru_{X/S,*}L(N)=N and E→L(E_D⊗Ω^•_{P/S}) a resolution for such P, and for S on which p is only locally nilpotent or p-adic; (c) the extension of L to PD differential operators and the identification of u_{X/S,*}L(E_D⊗Ω^•_{P/S}) with the de Rham complex (E_D⊗Ω^•_{P/S},∇). The source is Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, §6, which was not acquired.

gaps.title: Comparison with the de Rham complex of the envelope of a closed embedding
gaps.detail: Part (6): Stacks states the comparison with a de Rham complex globally only for a smooth lift (Remark 60.24.11, a remark with a hint of proof). That the restriction map of (5) to the PD envelope of a closed embedding agrees on affine opens with the quasi-isomorphism of Lemma 60.21.4 is asserted in that hint and not proved. The classical statement is Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, Theorem 7.1, a source that was not acquired.

gaps.title: Čech–Alexander and alternating Čech complexes over a cover (Stacks Remarks 60.24.3–60.24.4)
gaps.detail: The completion contract of the stage asks, for a cover of a separated X by affine opens with embeddings, for the Čech–Alexander totalization over multiple intersections and its independence of refinement. Stacks states this as Remarks 60.24.3 and 60.24.4 with hints only (the hint to 60.24.4 ends with 'insert future reference here'); no acquired source proves it. CR.3/crystalline-descent states the alternating version in general terms. Stacks Remark 60.24.4 has no written proof. Its hint reduces the claim to 'a general result in cohomology on sites, namely that the alternating Čech complex computes the cohomology provided it gives the correct answer on all the pieces (insert future reference here)'. Missing input: for a finite totally ordered covering of the final object of a ringed topos by subobjects U_λ and a bounded-below complex K of modules, the alternating Čech complex built from complexes computing RΓ(U_(λ₀)∩…∩U_(λ_n),K), λ₀<…<λ_n, computes RΓ(K). The missing input is requested from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2.

gaps.title: Independence of the embedding for smooth ambient schemes
gaps.detail: The stage asks for independence of the embedding for closed embeddings into smooth schemes, with explicit homotopies and Čech–Alexander totalizations over a cover. For two closed embeddings X→P₁, X→P₂ into smooth S-schemes that are not affine spaces, the fact that the PD envelope of X in P₁×_SP₂ is locally a PD polynomial algebra over each of the two envelopes is not in Stacks (Lemma 60.2.5 covers polynomial algebras only); the classical source, Berthelot–Ogus §§6–7, was not acquired. The Čech complexes of Stacks Remarks 60.24.3–60.24.4 are stated with hints only.

gaps.title: Filtered Poincaré lemma and filtered comparison
gaps.detail: The stage asks to compare filtrations. The comparison is: for a closed embedding X→P into a smooth S-scheme with PD envelope D, Ru_{X/S,*}(J_crys^{[r]}·F)≅Filʳ(F_D⊗Ω^•_{P/S}) compatibly in r, where J_crys^{[r]} are the PD powers of J_crys (API of CR.1/structure-sheaves); in particular Filʳ does not depend on the embedding, and for a smooth lift it is the filtration of (3). This is the filtered Poincaré lemma and the filtered comparison theorem of Berthelot–Ogus, Notes on Crystalline Cohomology, §§6–7, a source that was not acquired; the Stacks chapter contains no filtered statement.

gaps.title: Smooth-lift comparison (Stacks Remark 60.24.11)
gaps.detail: Part (1) is Stacks Remark 60.24.11, one of the results of §60.24 'whose proof is missing'; the hint (the map of CR.2/embedding-computation (5) is an isomorphism for affine X by Lemma 60.21.4) has to be written out, including the identification of that map with the quasi-isomorphism of the lemma.

gaps.title: Crystals on a proper smooth lift and Grothendieck existence (Stacks Remark 60.24.14)
gaps.detail: Part (1) is Stacks Remark 60.24.14, stated with a hint only: the existence of F_Y is referred to Grothendieck's existence theorem with '(insert future reference here)', and the algebraization of the connection, which is not O-linear, is not addressed. The argument through the first-order neighbourhood of the diagonal given in the proof steps has to be written out; no acquired source contains it.

gaps.title: Base change: envelope of a Koszul-regular sequence over a PD base, and Mayer–Vietoris (Stacks Remarks 60.24.2, 60.24.8, 60.24.9)
gaps.detail: Stacks Remarks 60.24.8 and 60.24.9 are stated with hints only. Not written out in any source read: (a) for a PD ring (A′,I′,γ′), P′=A′[x₁,…,x_n] and f′₁,…,f′_c∈P′ with Koszul-regular images in (A′/I′)[x], the PD envelope of I′P′+(f′_i) relative to γ′ is P′⟨ξ₁,…,ξ_c⟩/(ξ_i−f′_i) and ξ_i−f′_i is a Koszul-regular sequence in P′⟨ξ⟩ (the hint says 'Then you check that…'; Stacks Lemma 60.2.4 gives the further generators δ_n(Σr_iξ_i−r₀) of the kernel, which lie in (ξ_i−f′_i) because H₁ of the Koszul complex of the f̄′_i vanishes); (b) the Mayer–Vietoris triangle of Remark 60.24.2. CR.0/regular-envelope (0) gives the presentation of the envelope under its condition (K), which holds for Koszul-regular images; the Koszul-regularity of the ξ_i−f′_i in P′⟨ξ⟩ and the resulting isomorphism D′⊗^L_(A′)A≅D are not stated there.

gaps.title: Perfectness of proper smooth crystalline cohomology (Stacks Remarks 60.24.12–60.24.13)
gaps.detail: Stacks Remarks 60.24.12 and 60.24.13 are hints, not proofs; the proof steps of CR.3/proper-perfectness write the argument out. Its inputs are supplied or requested: perfectness of RΓ(X,F) for F finite locally free and X proper and flat (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.2/proper-perfect-pushforward-perfect over a Noetherian base; the statement with Tor-amplitude and base change is requested from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension), and Stacks, More on Algebra, Lemmas 07LU and 09AW (requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1). The non-Noetherian case of Remark 60.24.12 is not claimed.

gaps.title: Frobenius slopes of H¹ of an elliptic curve
gaps.detail: Not stated in CR.3 (it was the last clause of the old statement): for an elliptic curve E over k the Frobenius slopes of H¹_crys(E/W)[1/p] are {0,1} if E is ordinary and {1/2,1/2} if E is supersingular; equivalently, if E is ordinary H¹_crys(E/W) has an F-stable direct summand of rank one on which F is bijective and F is p times a bijection on the quotient, and if E is supersingular F²(H¹)=p·H¹. A proof without Dieudonné theory would need: (i) Λ²H¹≅H² through the cup product, giving F(Λ²H¹)=p·Λ²H¹; (ii) that F modulo p on H¹_dR(E/k) kills H⁰(E,Ω¹) and induces the Hasse–Witt map on H¹(E,O); (iii) [p]^*=p on H¹_crys(E/W) and a Verschiebung V with FV=VF=p; (iv) the equivalence of 'the Hasse–Witt map is non-zero' with the Tau Ceti definition 'E[p](k^sep)≠O', through 'V separable ⟺ V^*ω≠0' for the invariant differential ω; (v) the identification of the Tau Ceti Weierstrass curve with a smooth proper k-scheme and of ω with a generator of H⁰(E,Ω¹). Items (iv) and (v) are not statements of the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves layer 3 as described, and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2 cannot supply the comparison of H¹_crys with the Dieudonné module without depending on CR.3. The statement belongs in a stage that may require both CR.3 and R07.2 (CR.7 requires R07.2).

gaps.title: Curve inputs for crystalline cohomology of curves
gaps.detail: Parts (b) and (c) of CR.3/torsion-and-models use, beyond the Hodge numbers of a curve and Riemann–Roch (requested from the Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer B): the degeneration of the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence of a smooth proper curve over a field and over W_n (see the gap on the vanishing of d in top degree), and the existence of a smooth proper lift of C to W(k) (explicit for an elliptic curve, by deformation theory in general). The freeness of H²_crys(C/W) can instead be deduced from CR.3:duality/poincare-pairing (H²_tors≅Hom_W(H¹_tors,W[1/p]/W)=0), which a node of CR.3 cannot use.

gaps.title: Cohomological inputs for the torsion surface of BMS1 §2
gaps.detail: Part (d) uses, beyond the geometric construction of BMS1 Lemmas 2.5–2.9: crystalline higher direct images Rf_crys* with their Leray spectral sequence (Stacks Remark 60.24.1, a remark with hints), base change of R¹f_crys*O to a fibre for the E_k-torsor H_(E,k)→H_k, the computation of H^i_crys(X_(E,k)/W) through the projection to E_k/G_k with fibres P_k, and [p]^*=p on H¹_crys(E_k/W). None of these is a node of CR.0–CR.4. The existing gap 'BMS torsion-surface geometry and elliptic realization' names only the geometric input.

gaps.title: Identification with the crystalline trace of Berthelot
gaps.detail: The identification of Tr_X with the crystalline trace of Berthelot (LNM 407, VII 1.4.9) is not part of this node. Ekedahl I.5 derives it from LNM 407 VI Propositions 1.4.5 and 1.6.1 and VII Théorème 1.4.6 and 1.4.11, which were not available; the source says of this comparison that it 'will not be used anywhere else in this article'. The construction of the trace and the duality theorem do not depend on it.

gaps.title: Inputs of crystalline Poincaré duality
gaps.detail: Serre duality on X is supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/serre-proper, SF.2/smooth-proper and SF.2/trace; the vanishing of the coherent trace on d(H^d(X,Ω^(d−1)_X)) is a separate gap. Not supplied and not stated: (a) compatibility of Tr_X and of the pairing with an extension k→k′ of perfect fields, which the stage description asks for under "base-change"; it is not in Ekedahl. (b) The classical proof with coefficients (Berthelot, LNM 407, VII) was not available; the proof steps give the reduction to de Rham duality.

gaps.title: Gysin maps: cycle class and base change
gaps.detail: Not stated in this node, and not proved in any source read: (a) for a regular closed immersion f, the agreement of f_* with the local construction through crystalline residues and of f_*(1) with the cycle class of Berthelot, LNM 407, VI; (b) base change g^*∘f_*=f′_*∘g′^* for a cartesian square of proper smooth k-schemes X′=X×_Y Y′ with dim X′=dim X+dim Y′−dim Y. Both need the purity theorem of LNM 407 VI, which was not available. The stage description asks for 'functoriality and base-change' of the Gysin formalism; (b) is the missing part.

gaps.title: Trace of an external product
gaps.detail: Parts (3)–(5) use Tr_(X×Y)(pr₁^*x∪pr₂^*y)=Tr_X(x)·Tr_Y(y) for classes x, y of top degree (compatibility of the trace with products under the Künneth isomorphism). Neither Ekedahl nor another source read states it for the crystalline trace, and it is not an API item of CR.3:duality/trace. Part (2) does not use it.

gaps.title: Inputs of the seminormalisation theorem (Swan; Popescu for discrete valuation rings)
gaps.detail: For the new node CR.4/saturated-seminormalisation. Inputs of BLM §6.6 that no acquired source proves: (i) Swan, On seminormality (1980): existence of the seminormalisation as a universal map to a seminormal ring (Theorem 4.1) and the fact that a seminormal ring admits no proper integral extension that is bijective on k-points for all fields k (Lemma 2.6); (ii) Popescu's theorem for discrete valuation rings of characteristic p (they are filtered colimits of smooth F_p-algebras), used in BLM Proposition 6.6.8; for fields the corresponding statement is elementary (finitely generated field extensions of F_p are separably generated).

gaps.title: Witt vectors as the cofree δ-ring (Joyal)
gaps.detail: BLM Proposition 3.6.2 (second proof step of CR.4/saturated-de-rham-witt) uses two facts about Witt vectors. That W(S) is the cofree δ-ring on S (Joyal) is supplied by PrismaticCohomology:PR.0/delta-ring-category and PR.0/torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence, nodes of a packet that is not yet in the atlas. That W(S) is p-torsion-free with injective Frobenius when S is a reduced F_p-algebra is neither a node of a packet nor a declaration of the pinned Mathlib; it follows from p=V∘F on W(S), the injectivity of V and the formula F(x)_n=x_n^p in characteristic p.

gaps.title: Witt vectors of an étale map (BMS1 Theorem 10.4)
gaps.detail: BMS1 Theorem 10.4, used in proof step 1 and through this node by CR.4/torus-integral-part, CR.4/perfectoid-base-change and CR.4/crystalline-comparison: for an étale ring map A→B and r≥1, W_r(A)→W_r(B) is étale, and for every ring map A→A′ with B′=B⊗_A A′ the natural map W_r(A′)⊗_(W_r(A))W_r(B)→W_r(B′) is an isomorphism; no hypothesis on the rings. Proof route given by the source: for Z[1/p]-algebras W_r is a product of r copies of the ring by the ghost map; W_r commutes with localisation, which reduces to Z_(p)-algebras; for F-finite Z_(p)-algebras the statement is Langer–Zink Corollary A.18; the general case follows by writing B=B₀⊗_(A₀)A with A₀ finitely generated over Z_(p). The first part is van der Kallen, Theorem 2.4; the general result is Borger, Theorem 9.2 and Corollary 9.4. For F_p-algebras BLM Theorem 5.4.1 gives a direct proof by induction on r. No stage of the atlas owns this theorem; the promoted HabiroRings packet records the same statement for big Witt vectors as a gap ('Big Witt vectors of étale maps'). The draft roadmap QWittVectors (not in the atlas) lists étale base change of Witt vectors among the targets of its first layer.

gaps.title: Illusie's results on the classical complex of a smooth algebra
gaps.detail: Statement (1) of CR.4/classical-regular-comparison, for a smooth F_p-algebra R, uses results of Illusie on the classical complex that were read at the source for this review and are cited with their numbers in the proof steps: Théorème I.2.17, Proposition I.2.18 and 2.19 (the operator F on WΩ^*_R and the identities FV=VF=p, dF=pFd), Corollaire I.3.6 (WΩ^*_R is p-torsion-free), (I.3.21.1.5) (the image of F is d⁻¹(p·WΩ^*_R)) and Proposition I.3.31 (the kernel of WΩ^*_R→W_rΩ^*_R is V^rWΩ^*_R+dV^rWΩ^*_R; the citation of I.3.2 in BLM is recorded as a source issue). No node plans their proofs. For polynomial algebras they could be derived from CR.4/witt-basic-differentials (Langer–Zink Propositions 2.5, 2.6, 2.17, 2.19), but no node does so.

gaps.title: Popescu's theorem for regular Noetherian F_p-algebras
gaps.detail: Missing statement: every regular Noetherian F_p-algebra is a filtered colimit of smooth F_p-algebras (Popescu; Stacks Tag 07GB, as cited by BLM in the proofs of Theorems 4.3.1 and 4.4.12; Shiho Theorem 2.1 for regular local rings of characteristic p). CR.4/saturated-seminormalisation uses the case of discrete valuation rings of characteristic p (BLM Proposition 6.6.8). No node of any packet states it and no stage description of the atlas mentions it; the KTheoryFiniteLocalFields packet records the same statement as its gap "Popescu foundation for regular F_p comparisons". BLM give a proof of Theorem 4.3.1 that avoids Popescu (Corollary 9.5.19), but not of Theorem 4.4.12. A commutative-algebra foundation stage such as SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 is the natural owner (see restructure).

gaps.title: Slope spectral sequence: finiteness and degeneration
gaps.detail: The statement of CR.4/witt-slope-spectral-sequence was checked for this review against Illusie, Chapter II: Corollaire 2.5, Théorème 2.13, 3.1, Théorème 3.2 and Corollaire 3.5 (printed pp. 609–616); nothing from Illusie–Raynaud is needed for the statements after ⊗K. The proof steps use Théorème II.2.13 (H^b(X,WΩ^a_X) is of finite type modulo torsion, the torsion being killed by a power of p) and Corollaire II.2.5 (H^b(X,WΩ^a_X) is separated and complete for the V-adic topology) as cited results. No node plans their proofs; that of II.2.13 rests on a lemma of Bloch quoted in Illusie, Remarque II.2.12, and on Lemme II.2.14, which the source leaves as an exercise.

gaps.title: Zariski and étale images of the symbol map
gaps.detail: Comparison of the Zariski-local and étale-local images of the symbol map: Clausen–Mathew–Morrow (Definition 5.26) state, citing Morrow, K-theory and logarithmic Hodge–Witt sheaves of formal schemes in characteristic p, Corollary 4.1(iii), that the group of sections on an affine is the same whether the image is formed for the Zariski or for the étale topology. That paper is not acquired, and the node no longer asserts anything about the Zariski image.

gaps.title: Smooth cases of the logarithmic sequences
gaps.detail: For X smooth over F_p the proof steps of CR.4/logarithmic-witt-sequences derive (1) and (3) from Illusie I.3.3, I.3.4, I.3.26, I.3.28 and (I.5.7.4), and (2) is Illusie, Théorème I.5.7.2; these results were read at the source for this review and are used as cited results, and no node plans their proofs. Shiho quotes the smooth cases of (1) and (3) from Colliot-Thélène–Sansuc–Soulé, Torsion dans le groupe de Chow de codimension deux (1983), §1, Lemmes 2 and 3, a paper that was not acquired and is no longer needed. The reduction from regular to smooth schemes uses the theorem of Popescu (see the gap on it).

gaps.title: Hyodo–Kato complexes and the complex of Sato (cited by Disegni–Liu)
gaps.detail: Two inputs of this node are quoted, not proved, in the acquired source: (i) independence of Wω_X, Wω̃_X of the admissible embedding system and their identification with the modified de Rham–Witt complexes of Hyodo and Hyodo–Kato (Disegni–Liu p.82: 'It is well-known'; their references [27, 28]); (ii) Sato's cohomological de Rham–Witt complex WΞ_X∈D⁺(X_ét,W_•), which Disegni–Liu do not define: they cite [Sato, Definition 8.3], take from [Sato, Proposition 8.4] the equivalence ω⁺_X≃WΞ_(X,K₀) with ω⁺_X=Ru_*(Rs^⋆_*(Ξ^*_(Z^⋆)⊗O_(]X^⋆[))), Ξ^q=Ω^(q+1)_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)/Ω^(q+1)_(Z^⋆/W), and from [Sato, Proposition 8.10] the map Wω̃_X→WΞ_X[−1]. Sato's paper is not acquired, so WΞ_X is no longer part of this node's statement; CR.4/log-witt-proper-support uses it as cited data.

gaps.title: Comparison maps of Sato and the square (B.10)
gaps.detail: Sato's results used here are cited by Disegni–Liu and not acquired: the complex WΞ_X (Sato, Definition 8.3), the equivalence ω⁺_X≃WΞ_(X,K₀) (Proposition 8.4) and the map Wω̃_X→WΞ_X[−1] (Proposition 8.10). The commutativity of (B.10) needs in addition that Sato's map corresponds, under the two rational equivalences, to the map induced by the quotient maps Ω^(q+1)_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)→Ξ^q; Disegni–Liu display the square without proving this. The convergent objects ω̃_(U,X), ω⁺_(U,X) and the tube functor f^! have no owner (see the gap on tubes and convergent complexes).

gaps.title: Limits and the representability criterion for PD rings (Stacks Lemmas 23.3.2, 23.3.3)
gaps.detail: The existence of colimits of PD rings (Stacks Lemma 23.3.4) is proved in the source from two results that no node of the packet states and for which no pinned declaration was found: limits of PD rings exist and are computed on the underlying rings (Lemma 23.3.2), and a functor on PD rings that commutes with limits and satisfies a cardinality bound is representable (Lemma 23.3.3, an instance of the criterion of the chapter Categories). The pushout statements (1)–(3) of the node follow from the existence.

gaps.title: Frobenius between the crystalline sites over W_r(A) and W_(r−1)(A)
gaps.detail: The crystalline map 𝐅:Ru_(r*)O_(X/W_r(A))→Ru_((r−1)*)O_(X/W_(r−1)(A)) of the statement is not an instance of CR.3/frobenius-map, which is stated for one PD ring (A,I,γ) with p∈I, an endomorphism σ of it and a scheme over A/I. Three facts are used and stated by no node: (i) the divided powers of CR.4/witt-verschiebung-divided-powers extend to the kernel V W_(r−1)(A)+p·W_r(A) of W_r(A)→A/pA; (ii) F:W_r(A)→W_(r−1)(A) is a PD morphism for these ideals (F(γ_n(Vξ))=(p^n/n!)·ξ^n=γ_n(pξ) lies in p·W_(r−1)(A), not in V W_(r−2)(A)); (iii) Ru_*O for X over (W_r(A),V W_(r−1)(A)) agrees with that of X⊗F_p over the larger PD ideal, and crystalline cohomology is functorial for a PD morphism of bases covering the absolute Frobenius. Langer–Zink state the first two in a short passage before their Proposition 3.6.

gaps.title: Tubes, specialization and convergent log de Rham–Witt complexes (Disegni–Liu Appendix B)
gaps.detail: Missing objects and statements: for an admissible embedding system of a strictly semistable log scheme X of finite type over κ°, the tubes ]X^⋆[ in the generic fibres of the formal completions with their quasi-étale sites and the specialization maps s:]X^⋆[_qét→X^⋆_ét (Disegni–Liu B.1); the functor f^!_{(U,X)} (kernel of id→g_*g^* for g:]X∖U[→]X[, Definition B.1) with Lemma B.3; the complexes ω_X, ω̃_X, ω⁺_X and ω̃_{(U,X)}, ω⁺_{(U,X)} (B.2) with the comparison maps (B.5), (B.6), (B.9). No stage owns them: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3 has rigid tubes of frames and overconvergent isocrystals, without log structures, quasi-étale sites or specialization to the étale site. Sato's complex WΞ_X and its comparison maps, cited by Disegni–Liu, are also unsupplied.

gaps.title: Fixed points of an endofunctor of an ∞-category and their mapping spaces
gaps.detail: Missing construction and statement: for an ∞-category 𝒞 and a functor T:𝒞→𝒞, the fixed-point ∞-category 𝒞^T as the equalizer of id and T in ∞-categories, and for objects (X,φ_X), (Y,φ_Y) the identification of Map((X,φ_X),(Y,φ_Y)) with the equalizer of the two maps Map(X,Y)⇉Map(X,TY) (BLM Definition 7.4.3 and Remark 7.4.4, citing Nikolaus–Scholze, On topological cyclic homology, II.1.5). No node of any packet states it: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0/limits-colimits-and-slices is about limits inside a quasicategory, not limits of quasicategories, and a search for equalizers or limits of ∞-categories finds nothing. It can be a part of CR.4/leta-fixed-point or a node of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0 or E3.

gaps.title: Hodge and de Rham cohomology of projective space
gaps.detail: Missing statement: for a ring A and n≥1, H^q(P^n_A,Ω^p_{P^n_A/A})=0 unless 0≤p=q≤n, and H^p(P^n_A,Ω^p) is free of rank one, generated by the p-th power of the Hodge class of O(1); consequently H^{2i}_dR(P^n_A/A) is free of rank one on c₁^dR(O(1))^i for 0≤i≤n and the other de Rham cohomology groups vanish (Stacks, de Rham Cohomology, Lemmas 0FMI and 0FMJ). Used in part (a) of CR.3/torsion-and-models and in the normalisation of CR.3:duality/trace (proof steps 1, 4 and 6). No node of any packet states it (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3/projective-space-cohomology is étale, with torsion coefficients) and no stage description covers it: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension is about proper-flat coherent cohomology in general, the Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge layer B about curves, ComplexComparisonPartII:C1 about analytic O(n). The pinned libraries have no cohomology of projective space.

gaps.title: Vanishing of the de Rham differential on top-degree coherent cohomology
gaps.detail: Missing statement: for X smooth and proper over a field k, equidimensional of dimension d, the map d:H^d(X,Ω^{d−1}_{X/k})→H^d(X,Ω^d_{X/k}) is zero; equivalently the coherent trace t:H^d(X,Ω^d_{X/k})→k vanishes on exact classes and H^{2d}_dR(X/k)=H^d(X,Ω^d_{X/k}) (Stacks, de Rham Cohomology, Lemma 0FW6; its proof says that it does not follow formally from Serre duality and Lemma 0FW5, because d is not O_X-linear). Used by CR.3:duality/poincare-pairing (proof step 3), by statement (2) of CR.3:duality/trace, and for d=1 by CR.3/torsion-and-models (steps 2–3: the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence of a curve degenerates). No node of any packet states it; the promoted coherent-duality nodes of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 do not involve the de Rham differential, and the description of the JacobianChallenge layer B (genus, Riemann–Roch, Serre duality) does not cover it. Natural owner: the owner of coherent duality (see restructure).

signatureCoverage.meaning: Names of elaborated declarations and named examples are inventoried separately from omitted forms and typed components of wider contracts. Compilation checks types with proof placeholders; it does not certify mathematical proofs or the comment register. Regenerated by the independent review from the corrected packet and the suggested file: a node is typed when its declaration, every API item and every unit test has an elaborated declaration or labelled example of that name, partial when some have, omitted when none has. Typed does not say that the Lean statement is as strong as the statement of the node; the differences known to the review are listed in its report.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.Crystal
missing.statement: Let the site be CRIS(X/S) or Cris(X/S), ringed by O_crys. An O_crys-module E is a crystal in O_crys-modules if for every morphism f:(U,T,δ)→(U′,T′,δ′) the comparison map c_f:f^*E_T′=O_T⊗_{f⁻¹O_T′}f⁻¹E_T′→E_T is an isomorphism. It is a crystal in quasi-coherent modules, respectively of finite type, respectively in finite locally free modules, if moreover every restriction E_T is a quasi-coherent O_T-module, respectively quasi-coherent of finite type, respectively finite locally free. An O_crys-module is quasi-coherent as a module on the ringed site if and only if it is a crystal in quasi-coherent modules (Stacks Lemma 60.11.2). For O_crys-modules E, F one has (E⊗F)_T=E_T⊗_{O_T}F_T, and the tensor product of two crystals is a crystal; for a crystal E in finite locally free modules the dual E^∨=Hom(E,O_crys) is a crystal with (E^∨)_T=Hom_{O_T}(E_T,O_T). Crystals in finite locally free modules, with the sequences that are exact on every thickening, form a rigid tensor exact category; they are not closed under cokernels.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.Isocrystal
missing.statement: (Crystals and isocrystals over W.) Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k) and W_n=W/pⁿ with the canonical PD structure on (p), and Z a smooth k-scheme. Crys(Z/W_n) is the category of crystals of finite type on Cris(Z/Spec W_n), and Crys(Z/W) the category of crystals of finite type on Cris(Z/Spec W); every object of Cris(Z/Spec W) is Zariski locally an object of some Cris(Z/Spec W_n). The category of isocrystals is the ℚ-linearization Isoc(Z/W)=Crys(Z/W)_ℚ: the same objects, with Hom_Isoc(E,F)=Hom_Crys(E,F)⊗_ℤℚ (Esnault–Groechenig §2.6). Crystals in finite locally free modules form a full subcategory of Crys(Z/W); Isoc(Z/W) is formed from all crystals of finite type, not only from these. (F-crystals.) Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring with A a ℤ_(p)-algebra and p∈I, S=Spec A, σ:A→A a PD homomorphism with σ(x)≡xᵖ mod pA for all x∈A, and X→S₀=Spec A/I a morphism of schemes with p locally nilpotent on X (Stacks Situation 60.26.1). The absolute Frobenius F_X lies over Spec σ and gives (F_X)_cris:(X/S)_cris→(X/S)_cris. An F-crystal on X/S relative to σ is a pair (E,Φ) of a crystal E in finite locally free O_crys-modules and a map Φ:(F_X)_cris^*E→E. It is nondegenerate if there exist an integer i≥0 and a map V:E→(F_X)_cris^*E with V∘Φ=pⁱ·id (Stacks Definition 60.26.2). If the rank of E is at most r, then V′=p^{ri}V satisfies V′∘Φ=Φ∘V′=p^{ri+i}·id (Stacks Remark 60.26.3). The case A=W(k) or W_n(k), I=(p), σ the Frobenius of Witt vectors is the instance over a perfect field. (F-isocrystals.) For Z smooth over perfect k, (F_Z)_cris^* induces an endofunctor F^* of Isoc(Z/W); an F-isocrystal is an object E of Isoc(Z/W) with an isomorphism Φ:F^*E→E in Isoc(Z/W), and E has a Frobenius structure in the sense of Esnault–Groechenig if (F^*)^fE≅E for some integer f≥1.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.PDStratification
missing.statement: In Stacks Situation 60.5.1 (p a prime, (A,I,γ) a PD ring with A a ℤ_(p)-algebra, A→C a ring map with IC=0 and p nilpotent in C), let P=A[x_i] be a polynomial algebra with a surjection P→C of A-algebras, and for n≥0 let J(n) be the kernel of P⊗_A⋯⊗_AP→C (n+1 factors). D(n) is the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of J(n) relative to γ, and D=D(0). The D(n) form a cosimplicial object in PD rings, and D(n) is the coproduct of n+1 copies of D in the category Cris^∧(C/A) of p-adically complete PD thickenings of C (Stacks Remark 60.5.4, Lemma 60.17.2). Write p₀,p₁:D→D(1), q₀,q₁,q₂:D→D(2) and q₀₁,q₁₂,q₀₂:D(1)→D(2) for the coprojections and Δ:D(1)→D for the codiagonal. A PD stratification on a p-adically complete D-module M is a D(1)-linear isomorphism ε:M⊗^∧_{D,p₀}D(1)→M⊗^∧_{D,p₁}D(1) such that Δ^*ε=id_M and q₀₂^*ε=q₁₂^*ε∘q₀₁^*ε as maps M⊗^∧_{D,q₀}D(2)→M⊗^∧_{D,q₂}D(2). Here ⊗^∧ is the p-adically completed tensor product.

One has θ_0=id and θ_K∘θ_L=θ_{K+L}; so the θ_i=θ_{e_i} commute and θ_K=∏_iθ_i^{k_i} (proof of Stacks Lemma 60.17.3).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.envelopeDifferentials
missing.statement: Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring, A→P a ring map, J⊂P an ideal with IP⊂J, and (D,J̄,γ̄)=D_{P,γ}(J) the PD envelope. The canonical map Ω_{P/A}⊗_PD→Ω¹_PD(D/A) is an isomorphism (Stacks Lemma 60.6.6); no flatness of D over P is needed. Hence Ω^q_PD(D/A)=Ω^q_{P/A}⊗_PD for every q≥0. If P is smooth over A these D-modules are finite locally free. If p is a prime, A is a ℤ_(p)-algebra and p is nilpotent in P/J, then with D_e=D/pᵉD the p-adic completion of Ω¹_PD(D/A) is lim_eΩ¹_PD(D_e/A) (Stacks Lemma 60.6.10); for P=A[x_i] it consists of the sums Σf_idx_i with f_i in the p-adic completion D^∧ of D and, for every e, f_i∈pᵉD^∧ for all but finitely many i.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crystalConnectionEquivalence
missing.statement: Convention. A PD stratification is ε:M⊗^∧_{D,p₀}D(1)→M⊗^∧_{D,p₁}D(1) (CR.1/pd-stratification), a connection is written ∇m=Σ_iθ_i(m)dx_i (CR.1/quasi-nilpotent-connection), and ξ_i=x_i⊗1−1⊗x_i=p₀(x_i)−p₁(x_i)∈D(1). (1) In Stacks Situation 60.5.1 with X=Spec C and S=Spec A, let P=A[x_i]→C be a surjection from a polynomial algebra, D the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of its kernel and D_e=D/pᵉD. For a crystal F in quasi-coherent O_crys-modules on Cris(X/S), M=lim_eΓ((X,Spec D_e,γ̄),F) is a p-adically complete D-module with M/pᵉM=Γ((X,Spec D_e,γ̄),F), the crystal property gives a PD stratification ε on M, and ε(m⊗1)=Σ_Kθ_K(m)⊗∏_iξ_i^{[k_i]} with θ_K=∏_iθ_i^{k_i}, where ∇(m)=Σ_iθ_i(m)dx_i is the canonical connection of F evaluated on the Spec D_e; ∇ is integrable and topologically quasi-nilpotent (Stacks Lemma 60.17.3). (2) The functor F↦(M,∇) is an equivalence from the category of crystals in quasi-coherent O_crys-modules on Cris(X/S) to the category of pairs (M,∇) of a p-adically complete D-module and an integrable, topologically quasi-nilpotent connection ∇:M→M⊗^∧_DΩ_D (Stacks Proposition 60.17.4). A quasi-inverse sends (M,∇) to the crystal with value M⊗_{D,f}B on an affine object (U,Spec B,δ) with a morphism f:D→B of thickenings, two choices f, g being identified by c_{f,g}(m⊗1)=Σ_Kθ_K(m)⊗∏_i(f(x_i)−g(x_i))^{[k_i]}, a finite sum. (3) Let A→P′→C be ring maps with P′ smooth over A and P′→C surjective with kernel J′, and D′ the p-adic completion of D_{P′,γ}(J′). There are a surjection P→C from a polynomial algebra and PD A-algebra maps a:D→D′, b:D′→D compatible with the maps to C with a∘b=id; base change along a and b gives an equivalence between the pairs (M,∇) over D and the pairs (M′,∇′) over D′ that are p-adically complete, integrable and topologically quasi-nilpotent, and the equivalence of (2) holds for the functor F↦(M′,∇′) (Stacks Lemma 60.17.5).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.finiteWittEvaluation
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k) with the canonical PD structure on (p), W_n=W/pⁿ, Z a smooth k-scheme of finite type and Ẑ a smooth p-adic formal W-scheme with Ẑ⊗_Wk=Z; put Z_n=Ẑ⊗_WW_n. Then (Z,Z_n,γ) is an object of Cris(Z/Spec W_n). Let MIC(Z_n) be the category of O_{Z_n}-modules of finite type with an integrable connection ∇_n:E_n→E_n⊗Ω¹_{Z_n/W_n}. Call (E_n,∇_n) quasi-nilpotent if for every affine open Spec P′ of Z_n the pair (Γ(Spec P′,E_n),∇_n) over D′=P′ is topologically quasi-nilpotent in the sense of CR.1/quasi-nilpotent-connection (Stacks Lemma 60.17.5), and let MIC(Z_n)^qn be the full subcategory of these. (1) Evaluation E↦(E_{Z_n},∇) on the object (Z,Z_n,γ) is an equivalence from Crys(Z/W_n), the crystals of finite type on Cris(Z/Spec W_n), to MIC(Z_n)^qn, compatible with reduction from W_{n+1} to W_n; crystals in finite locally free modules correspond to the (E_n,∇_n) with E_n finite locally free. (2) (E_n,∇_n) in MIC(Z_n) is quasi-nilpotent if and only if its reduction (E_1,∇_1)=(E_n,∇_n)⊗_{W_n}k is. (3) Crys(Z/W) is equivalent to the category of coherent O_Ẑ-modules E with an integrable connection such that (E,∇)⊗_WW_n lies in MIC(Z_n)^qn for every n; such E satisfy E=lim_nE/pⁿE.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.RΓcrys
missing.statement: In the situation of CR.1/crystalline-site, with f:X→S the structure map, u_{X/S}:(X/S)_cris→Sh(X_Zar) is a morphism of topoi (CR.1/site-morphisms). It is not a morphism of ringed topoi to (X_Zar,O_X): the natural ring map goes from O_crys to u⁻¹O_X. Through u⁻¹f⁻¹O_S→O_crys every O_crys-module is a module over u⁻¹f⁻¹O_S, and Ru_{X/S,*}:D((X/S)_cris,O_crys)→D(X_Zar,f⁻¹O_S) is the derived direct image. Crystalline cohomology is RΓ_crys(X/S,E)=RΓ(Cris(X/S),E)=RΓ(X_Zar,Ru_{X/S,*}E), an object of D(Γ(S,O_S)). In particular, for a PD ring (A,I,γ) with A a ℤ_(p)-algebra and p nilpotent in A/I, S=Spec A and X an S₀-scheme with p locally nilpotent on X, RΓ_crys(X/S,E)∈D(A) is defined although p need not be nilpotent in A. In that case pᵉA⊂I is stable under γ for e≫0; with S_e=Spec A/pᵉA, Cris(X/S_e) is a full subcategory of Cris(X/S), and for every O_crys-module F with restrictions F_e to Cris(X/S_e) one has RΓ(Cris(X/S),F)≅Rlim_eRΓ(Cris(X/S_e),F_e) (Stacks Remark 60.24.10).

For every A-module N the complex 0→N→N⊗_AP→N⊗_AΩ¹_PD(P/A)→N⊗_AΩ²_PD(P/A)→⋯ is exact (Stacks Lemma 60.20.1). (2) Let (B,I,δ) be a PD ring with B an A-algebra, P=B⟨x_i⟩_{i∈W} with PD ideal IP+P₊, and M a B-module with an integrable connection ∇:M→M⊗_BΩ¹_PD(B/A). Then the map of de Rham complexes M⊗_BΩ^•_PD(B/A)→M⊗_BΩ^•_PD(P/A) is a quasi-isomorphism (Stacks Lemma 60.20.2). (3) Let p be a prime. In (1), with D₀ the p-adic completion of P and Ωⁱ_{D₀} the p-adic completion of Ωⁱ_PD(P/A), the complex 0→N→N⊗^∧_AD₀→N⊗^∧_AΩ¹_{D₀}→⋯ is exact for every p-adically complete A-module N. In (2), with D and D′ the p-adic completions of B and P and Ωⁱ_D, Ωⁱ_{D′} the p-adic completions of Ωⁱ_PD(B/A) and Ωⁱ_PD(P/A), the map M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_D→M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_{D′} is a quasi-isomorphism for every p-adically complete D-module M with an integrable connection ∇:M→M⊗^∧_DΩ¹_D. (4) For one variable z over B the contraction is explicit: on Ω^•_PD(B⟨z⟩/B), the B-linear map h with h(z^{[n]}dz)=z^{[n+1]} and h=0 in degree 0 satisfies dh+hd=id−ev₀, where ev₀ is evaluation at z=0 in degree 0 and zero in degree 1 (Stacks Example 60.25.2).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysEmbeddingComputation
missing.statement: Setting for (1)–(4): Stacks Situation 60.5.1 with X=Spec C and S=Spec A, P=A[x_i]→C a surjection from a polynomial algebra, D(n) the p-adically completed PD envelopes of CR.1/pd-stratification, D=D(0), and T(n)_e=Spec D(n)/pᵉD(n), so that (X,T(n)_e,γ̄) is an object of Cris(X/S) for e≫0. (1) (Čech–Alexander complex.) Let F be an O_crys-module on Cris(X/S) such that every restriction F_T is quasi-coherent and c_f:f^*F_T′→F_T is surjective for every morphism of Cris(X/S) with f:T→T′ a closed immersion. Then M(n)=lim_eΓ((X,T(n)_e,γ̄),F) is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial ring D(•), and the complex M(0)→M(1)→M(2)→⋯ computes RΓ(Cris(X/S),F) (Stacks Proposition 60.21.1). (2) For such F, Hʲ(Cris(X/S),F⊗_{O_crys}Ωⁱ_{X/S})=0 for all i>0 and j≥0 (Stacks Lemma 60.21.2). (3) If F is a crystal in quasi-coherent modules and (M,∇) the associated module with connection over D (CR.1/taylor-equivalence), then M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_D computes RΓ(Cris(X/S),F) (Stacks Proposition 60.21.3); if p is nilpotent in A the completions may be omitted. (4) If A→P′→C are ring maps with P′ smooth over A and P′→C surjective, D′ is the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of the kernel and (M′,∇′) is the pair over D′ associated to F, then M′⊗^∧_{D′}Ω^•_{D′} computes RΓ(Cris(X/S),F) (Stacks Lemma 60.21.4). (5) (Sheaf form.) In the situation of CR.1/crystalline-site, for a crystal F in quasi-coherent modules, Ru_{X/S,*}(F⊗_{O_crys}Ωⁱ_{X/S})=0 for all i>0, so the map of complexes F⊗Ω^•_{X/S}→F[0] becomes an isomorphism after Ru_{X/S,*} (Stacks Proposition 60.23.1); for every object (U,T,δ) this gives a canonical map RΓ(Cris(X/S),F)→RΓ(T,F_T⊗_{O_T}Ω^•_{T/S,δ}). (6) (Closed embedding.) If moreover p is locally nilpotent on S and X→P is a closed S₀-immersion into a smooth S-scheme with PD envelope D, then (X,D,γ̄) is an object of Cris(X/S) and the map of (5) for T=D induces an isomorphism Ru_{X/S,*}F≅F_D⊗_{O_P}Ω^•_{P/S} in D(X_Zar,f⁻¹O_S).

(1) For every PD A-algebra endomorphism ρ:D→D compatible with the maps to C, the induced map M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_D→M⊗^∧_{D,ρ}Ω^•_D is a quasi-isomorphism (proof of Stacks Lemma 60.21.4). (2) For ring maps A→P′→C with P′ smooth and P′→C surjective, a surjection P→P′ from a polynomial algebra and a:D→D′, b:D′→D as in CR.1/taylor-equivalence (3), the base change maps M′⊗^∧_{D′}Ω^•_{D′}→M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_D along b and M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_D→M′⊗^∧_{D′}Ω^•_{D′} along a are quasi-isomorphisms (Stacks Lemma 60.21.4). (3) Each of the b+1 coprojections D→D(b) induces a quasi-isomorphism M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_D→M⊗^∧_DΩ^•_{D(b)}, and they all induce the same map in the derived category, the inverse being induced by the codiagonal D(b)→D (proof of Stacks Proposition 60.21.3). (4) Let P₁→C and P₂→C be surjections from polynomial A-algebras, with completed envelopes D₁, D₂, and D₁₂ the completed envelope of the kernel of P₁⊗_AP₂→C, and let (M₁,∇), (M₂,∇), (M₁₂,∇) be the modules with connection of F. Then D₁₂ is the p-adic completion of a PD polynomial algebra over D₁ and over D₂, and the maps M₁⊗^∧Ω^•_{D₁}→M₁₂⊗^∧Ω^•_{D₁₂}←M₂⊗^∧Ω^•_{D₂} are quasi-isomorphisms compatible with the identifications of the three complexes with RΓ(Cris(X/S),F). (5) Any two PD A-algebra maps g,h:D₂→D₁ compatible with the maps to C induce the same map M₂⊗^∧Ω^•_{D₂}→M₁⊗^∧Ω^•_{D₁} in the derived category.

missing.statement: (1) (Smooth lift; Stacks Remark 60.24.11.) Let p be a prime, (A,I,γ) a PD ring with p nilpotent in A, S=Spec A, S₀=Spec A/I, Y a smooth S-scheme, X=Y×_SS₀, and F a crystal in quasi-coherent O_crys-modules on Cris(X/S). Then γ extends to a PD structure on the ideal of X in Y, so that (X,Y,γ) is an object of Cris(X/S); the restriction F_Y carries a canonical integrable connection ∇:F_Y→F_Y⊗_{O_Y}Ω_{Y/S}; and RΓ(Cris(X/S),F)≅RΓ(Y,F_Y⊗_{O_Y}Ω^•_{Y/S}) in D(A). (2) (Filtration on an envelope.) Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring, P an A-algebra, J⊂P an ideal containing IP, (D,J̄,γ̄) the PD envelope and J̄^{[a]} the PD powers of J̄ (CR.0/pd-filtration), with J̄^{[a]}=D for a≤0. Then d(J̄^{[a]})⊂J̄^{[a−1]}·Ω¹_PD(D/A). Hence for every integer r the submodules Filʳ(Ω^q_PD(D/A))=J̄^{[r−q]}·Ω^q_PD(D/A) form a subcomplex Filʳ of Ω^•_PD(D/A), decreasing in r, equal to the whole complex for r≤0; and for a D-module M with integrable connection the submodules J̄^{[r−q]}·(M⊗_DΩ^q_PD(D/A)) form a subcomplex of M⊗_DΩ^•_PD(D/A). (3) If I=0 and J=0, so that D=P, then Filʳ=σ_{≥r}Ω^•_{P/A}, the stupid truncation. In the situation of (1), for D=O_Y and J̄=IO_Y, the image of Filʳ in Ω^•_{X/S₀} is σ_{≥r}Ω^•_{X/S₀}.

Let p be a prime, (A,I,γ) a PD ring with A noetherian and p-adically complete and p nilpotent in A/I, S=Spec A, S₀=Spec A/I, Y a proper smooth S-scheme, X=Y×_SS₀, and F a crystal of finite type in quasi-coherent O_crys-modules on Cris(X/S). Then there is a coherent O_Y-module F_Y with an integrable connection ∇:F_Y→F_Y⊗_{O_Y}Ω_{Y/S} such that F_Y/pᵉF_Y with its connection is the module with connection over A/pᵉA of CR.2/smooth-lift-filtration (1), and RΓ(Cris(X/S),F)≅RΓ(Y,F_Y⊗_{O_Y}Ω^•_{Y/S}) in D(A). (2) For A=W(k) with k a perfect field, I=(p) and K=W(k)[1/p]: RΓ(Cris(X/S),F)⊗_{W(k)}K≅RΓ(Y_K,F_{Y_K}⊗Ω^•_{Y_K/K}). (3) (Trace-free endomorphisms.) Let E be a crystal in finite locally free O_crys-modules of constant rank r≥1. The trace tr:End(E)=E^∨⊗E→O_crys is a surjective map of crystals, End⁰(E):=Ker(tr) is a crystal in finite locally free modules of rank r²−1, and (1) and (2) apply to End(E) and End⁰(E). The map O_crys⊕End⁰(E)→End(E), (a,φ)↦a·id+φ, has cokernel O_crys/r·O_crys; it is an isomorphism if p does not divide r, and it is not surjective if p divides r and X is nonempty.

Choose a finite affine open cover X=⋃_(λ∈Λ)U_λ with U_λ=Spec C_λ, a total order on Λ, and for each λ a surjection P_λ→C_λ from a polynomial A-algebra. For λ₀<…<λ_n write U_(λ₀)∩…∩U_(λ_n)=Spec C_(λ₀…λ_n), let D_(λ₀…λ_n) be the PD envelope, relative to γ, of the kernel of P_(λ₀)⊗_A…⊗_A P_(λ_n)→C_(λ₀…λ_n), and let (M_(λ₀…λ_n),∇) be the D_(λ₀…λ_n)-module with integrable connection attached to E. missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysBaseChange_id
missing.statement: For the identity of (A,I,γ) and the identity of X the base-change map K⊗^L_A A→K is the canonical isomorphism.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysBaseChange_comp
missing.statement: For PD homomorphisms (A″,I″,γ″)→(A′,I′,γ′)→(A,I,γ) and morphisms X→X′→X″ over them, the base-change map K″⊗^L_(A″)A→K is the composite of (K″⊗^L_(A″)A′)⊗^L_(A′)A→K′⊗^L_(A′)A with K′⊗^L_(A′)A→K.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysBaseChange_natural
missing.statement: A homomorphism E′₁→E′₂ of O_crys-modules on X′/S′ induces a commutative square of base-change maps; the base-change map is also natural for morphisms g:Y′→X′ of schemes over A′/I′ and their base changes.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysPerfect
missing.statement: (1) Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring with A Noetherian and p nilpotent in A, X a proper smooth scheme over A/I and E a finite locally free crystal on X/Spec A. Then K=RΓ_crys(X/Spec A,E) is a perfect complex of A-modules. (2) Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring with A Noetherian and p-adically complete and p nilpotent in A/I, X proper smooth over A/I and E a finite locally free crystal on X/Spec A. For e such that p^eA⊂I is stable under γ (all sufficiently large e) put K_e=RΓ_crys(X/Spec(A/p^e),E). Then K=Rlim_e K_e is a perfect complex of A-modules and K⊗^L_A A/p^e→K_e is an isomorphism for every such e. (3) Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, A=W(k), I=(p), X proper smooth over k of dimension ≤d and E a finite locally free crystal on X/W(k). Then K=RΓ_crys(X/W(k),E) is a perfect complex of W(k)-modules of Tor-amplitude in [0,2d], K⊗^L_(W(k))W_n(k)≅RΓ_crys(X/W_n(k),E) for all n≥1, and each H^i(K) is a finitely generated W(k)-module, zero unless 0≤i≤2d. The modules H^i(K) can have p-torsion. (4) In the situation of (2), for a homomorphism (A,I,γ)→(B,J,δ) of PD rings with B Noetherian and p-adically complete and p nilpotent in B/J, the base-change map K⊗^L_A B→RΓ_crys(X_B/Spec B,E_B) of CR.3/derived-base-change is an isomorphism, where X_B=X×_(Spec A/I)Spec B/J and E_B is the pullback of E.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup
missing.statement: Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring with A a Z_(p)-algebra, S=Spec A, X a scheme over A/I on which p is locally nilpotent, and write K(E)=RΓ_crys(X/S,E) for an O_crys-module E. (1) For O_crys-modules E, F the cup product is the map ∪:K(E)⊗^L_A K(F)→K(E⊗_(O_crys)F) in D(A) obtained from the cup product RΓ(E)⊗^L RΓ(F)→RΓ(E⊗^L_(O_crys)F) of the ringed crystalline topos followed by E⊗^L F→E⊗F; the unit is A→K(O_crys). (2) It is associative and unital, natural in E and F, and compatible with pullback along the morphisms of crystalline topoi induced by commutative squares of schemes over homomorphisms of PD rings. (3) On H^*_crys(X/S)=H^*(K(O_crys)) it is a graded A-algebra structure, graded commutative: x∪y=(−1)^(ij)·y∪x for x∈H^i, y∈H^j. In particular 2·x∪x=0 for x of odd degree, hence x∪x=0 when p is odd; for p=2 this gives only 2·x∪x=0. (4) For schemes X, Y over A/I the external product of x∈H^*(K_X(E)) and y∈H^*(K_Y(F)) is pr₁^*x∪pr₂^*y∈H^*(K_(X×Y)(pr₁^*E⊗pr₂^*F)), X×Y the fibre product over A/I.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_unit
missing.statement: The class 1∈H⁰_crys(X/S), image of 1 under the unit A→K(O_crys), satisfies 1∪x=x=x∪1 for x∈H^*(K(E)), under O_crys⊗E≅E≅E⊗O_crys.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_graded_comm
missing.statement: For x∈H^i_crys(X/S) and y∈H^j_crys(X/S): x∪y=(−1)^(ij)·y∪x; for O_crys-modules E, F the same holds between K(E⊗F) and K(F⊗E) through the exchange isomorphism.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_reduction
missing.statement: For a homomorphism of PD rings (A′,I′,γ′)→(A,I,γ) and f:X→X′ over it, the base-change map K′(E′)⊗^L_(A′)A→K(f_crys^*E′) of CR.3/derived-base-change is compatible with cup products and units. In particular, for p^eA⊂I stable under γ, the reduction K(E)→RΓ_crys(X/Spec(A/p^e),E) carries cup products to cup products.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_assoc
missing.statement: (x∪y)∪z=x∪(y∪z) in H^*(K(E⊗F⊗G)) for x∈H^*(K(E)), y∈H^*(K(F)), z∈H^*(K(G)); the same holds for the maps of complexes in D(A).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_pullback
missing.statement: For a morphism g:X′→X of schemes over a homomorphism of PD rings and O_crys-modules E, F on X: g^*(x∪y)=g^*x∪g^*y and g^*1=1.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_deRham
missing.statement: If p is nilpotent in A and Y is a smooth lift of X over A, then under H^*_crys(X/S)≅H^*(Y,Ω^•_(Y/A)) of CR.2/smooth-lift-filtration the cup product is the product induced by the wedge product of Ω^•_(Y/A); with coefficients it is induced by (e⊗ω)∧(f⊗η)=(e⊗f)⊗(ω∧η).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysCup_external
missing.statement: For schemes X, Y over A/I and classes x∈H^*(K_X(E)), y∈H^*(K_Y(F)): x⊠y=pr₁^*x∪pr₂^*y∈H^*(K_(X×Y)(pr₁^*E⊗pr₂^*F)); on complexes, K_X(E)⊗^L_A K_Y(F)→K_(X×Y)(pr₁^*E⊗pr₂^*F).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysCup_point
missing.statement: For X=Spec k, k a perfect field of characteristic p, and S=Spec W(k): K(O_crys)=W(k) in degree 0 and the cup product is the multiplication of W(k).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysCup_P1
missing.statement: On P¹×P¹ over a perfect field k, with h_a=pr_a^*h and h=c₁(O(1))∈H²_crys(P¹/W(k)): h₁∪h₂=h₂∪h₁ generates H⁴_crys(P¹×P¹/W(k))≅W(k), and h₁∪h₁=0=h₂∪h₂.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysCup_P2
missing.statement: On P² over a perfect field k: h∪h generates H⁴_crys(P²/W(k))≅W(k) and h∪h∪h=0, for h=c₁(O(1)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysCup_odd
missing.statement: For a geometrically connected smooth proper curve C over a perfect field k and x,y∈H¹_crys(C/W(k)): x∪y=−y∪x and x∪x=0 in H²_crys(C/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysKunneth
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k), X and Y proper smooth k-schemes and E, F finite locally free crystals on X/W and Y/W; write K(X,E)=RΓ_crys(X/W,E). The external cup product K(X,E)⊗^L_W K(Y,F)→K(X×_kY,pr₁^*E⊗pr₂^*F), x⊗y↦pr₁^*x∪pr₂^*y, is an isomorphism in D(W). It is compatible with cup products, with the reductions ⊗^L_W W_n(k), and, when (E,Φ_E) and (F,Φ_F) are F-crystals relative to the Witt vector Frobenius σ, with the linearised Frobenius maps of CR.3/frobenius-map for (E,Φ_E), (F,Φ_F) and (pr₁^*E⊗pr₂^*F,Φ_E⊗Φ_F). Consequently there are short exact sequences 0→⊕_(i+j=n)H^i(K(X,E))⊗_W H^j(K(Y,F))→H^n(K(X×Y,pr₁^*E⊗pr₂^*F))→⊕_(i+j=n+1)Tor₁^W(H^i(K(X,E)),H^j(K(Y,F)))→0.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius
missing.statement: Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring with A a Z_(p)-algebra and p∈I, and σ:A→A a homomorphism of PD rings with σ(x)≡x^p modulo pA. Let S=Spec A, S₀=Spec A/I and X an S₀-scheme. (1) The absolute Frobenius F_X of X lies over the absolute Frobenius F_(S₀) of S₀, which Spec(σ) lifts; it induces a morphism of crystalline topoi (F_X)_crys:(X/S)_crys→(X/S)_crys. (2) An F-crystal on X/S relative to σ is a crystal E in finite locally free O_crys-modules together with a map Φ:(F_X)_crys^*E→E; it is nondegenerate if there are an integer i≥0 and a map V:E→(F_X)_crys^*E with V∘Φ=p^i. The structure sheaf with the canonical isomorphism (F_X)_crys^*O_crys=O_crys is an F-crystal. (3) For an F-crystal (E,Φ) and K=RΓ_crys(X/S,E) the linearised Frobenius F_K:K⊗^L_(A,σ)A→K is the composite of three maps: the base-change map K⊗^L_(A,σ)A→RΓ_crys(X^(1)/S,E^(1)), where X^(1)=X×_(S₀,F_(S₀))S₀ and E^(1) is the pullback of E along the projection X^(1)→X over Spec(σ); the pullback RΓ_crys(X^(1)/S,E^(1))→RΓ_crys(X/S,(F_X)_crys^*E) along the relative Frobenius F_(X/S₀):X→X^(1); and the map induced by Φ. (4) The composite F:K→K⊗^L_(A,σ)A→K is σ-semilinear on cohomology: F(ax)=σ(a)F(x).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_semilinear
missing.statement: The endomorphism F of H^*(K) induced by K→K⊗^L_(A,σ)A→K is additive and satisfies F(ax)=σ(a)·F(x) for a∈A.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_linearize
missing.statement: F_K:K⊗^L_(A,σ)A→K is an A-linear map in D(A), the composite of the base-change map for Spec(σ), the pullback along the relative Frobenius F_(X/S₀):X→X^(1) and the map induced by Φ.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_lift
missing.statement: Assume p is nilpotent in A. Let Y be a smooth lift of X over A and φ̃:Y→Y a morphism over Spec(σ) whose reduction modulo p is the absolute Frobenius of Y⊗_A A/p. Under RΓ_crys(X/S)≅RΓ(Y,Ω^•_(Y/A)) of CR.2/smooth-lift-filtration the semilinear Frobenius of the structure crystal is induced by φ̃^*:Ω^•_(Y/A)→Ω^•_(Y/A), and φ̃^*(Ω^q_(Y/A))⊂p^q·Ω^q_(Y/A) for every q≥0.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_natural
missing.statement: For a morphism g:X′→X of schemes over A/I and a morphism of F-crystals g_crys^*(E,Φ)→(E′,Φ′), the induced map K→K′ commutes with the linearised Frobenius maps; in particular g^*∘F=F∘g^* on H^*_crys.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_cup
missing.statement: For F-crystals (E,Φ_E), (E′,Φ_(E′)) and the F-crystal (E⊗E′,Φ_E⊗Φ_(E′)): F(x∪y)=F(x)∪F(y); and F(1)=1 in H⁰_crys(X/S).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_chern
missing.statement: F(c₁(L))=p·c₁(L) in H²_crys(X/S) for every invertible O_X-module L, because F_X^*L≅L^(⊗p).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobenius_finite_field
missing.statement: For k=F_(p^f), A=W(k) and σ the Witt vector Frobenius, the iterate F^f is W(k)-linear on H^*_crys(X/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysFrobenius_point
missing.statement: For X=Spec k, k perfect of characteristic p, A=W(k), σ the Witt vector Frobenius: K=W(k) and F=σ; it is not W(k)-linear when k≠F_p.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysFrobenius_P1
missing.statement: For P¹ over a perfect field k and A=W(k): F=σ on H⁰_crys=W and F(h)=p·h for h=c₁(O(1))∈H²_crys(P¹/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysFrobenius_Pd
missing.statement: On H^(2i)_crys(P^d/W(k))=W·h^i, k perfect: F(a·h^i)=σ(a)·p^i·h^i for 0≤i≤d.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysFrobenius_singular
missing.statement: For X=Spec F_p[x,y]/(x²,xy,y²), A=Z_p with I=(p) and σ=id: the Frobenius F of H⁰_crys(X/Z_p) is not injective.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysWeakLefschetz
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, X a smooth projective variety of dimension d over k and L an invertible O_X-module. Let i_L≥0 be an integer such that for every coherent O_X-module F one has H^i(X,F⊗L^n)=0 for all i>i_L and all sufficiently large n. Then there is an integer n₀ such that for every n≥n₀ and every smooth H⊂X that is the zero scheme of a section of L^n, the restriction map H^j_crys(X/W(k))→H^j_crys(H/W(k)) is an isomorphism for j<d−i_L−1 and is injective with torsion-free cokernel for j=d−i_L−1. If L is ample one can take i_L=0.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysAcceptanceModels
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k), σ its Frobenius and F the semilinear Frobenius of CR.3/frobenius-map. (a) For d≥0: H^*_crys(P^d_k/W)=W[h]/(h^(d+1)) as a graded W-algebra, with h=c₁(O(1)) in degree 2; thus H^(2i)=W·h^i for 0≤i≤d, the odd groups vanish, and F(h)=p·h. (b) For a geometrically connected smooth proper curve C of genus g over k: H⁰_crys(C/W)=W, H¹_crys(C/W) is free of rank 2g, H²_crys(C/W) is free of rank 1, and F(H²_crys(C/W))=p·H²_crys(C/W). (c) For an elliptic curve E over k with origin 0: H¹_crys(E/W) is free of rank 2 and H²_crys(E/W)=W·e with e=c₁(O_E([0])) and F(e)=p·e. (d) Let O be the ring of integers of a complete algebraically closed non-archimedean extension C of Q_p, with residue field k. The smooth projective surface H over O constructed in BMS1 §2.2 satisfies H¹_crys(H_k/W(k))=0 and H²_crys(H_k/W(k))_tors≅k⊕k, while H²_ét(H_C,Z_p)_tors≅Z/p².

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysInseparableControl
missing.statement: Let (S,I,γ) be a PD scheme over Z_(p) with p∈I, S₀=V(I), and f:X′→X a morphism of S₀-schemes which, locally on X, is a composite of finitely many morphisms of the form Spec C[z]/(z^p−c)→Spec C (an iterated α_p-cover), of constant degree q. Let E be a crystal in quasi-coherent O_crys-modules on X/S and E′=f_crys^*E. Then the cone Q of Ru_(X/S,*)E→f_*Ru_(X′/S,*)E′ in the derived category of X_Zar has cohomology sheaves annihilated by q, and f^*:H^i_crys(X/S,E)→H^i_crys(X′/S,E′) has kernel and cokernel annihilated by q^(i+1). If X→S₀ is smooth of relative dimension d and X^(1)=X×_(S₀,F_(S₀))S₀, the relative Frobenius F_(X/S₀):X→X^(1) is an iterated α_p-cover of degree p^d; hence for every crystal G in quasi-coherent modules on X^(1)/S the map F_(X/S₀)^*:H^i_crys(X^(1)/S,G)→H^i_crys(X/S,(F_(X/S₀))_crys^*G) has kernel and cokernel annihilated by p^(d(i+1)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysFrobeniusIsogeny
missing.statement: Let (A,I,γ) be a PD ring with A Noetherian and p-adically complete and p∈I, σ:A→A a homomorphism of PD rings with σ(x)≡x^p modulo pA, X a proper smooth scheme over A/I, and (E,Φ) a nondegenerate F-crystal on X/Spec A relative to σ: E is a crystal in finite locally free O_crys-modules, Φ:(F_X)_crys^*E→E, and there are an integer i≥0 and a map V:E→(F_X)_crys^*E with V∘Φ=p^i. Then the linearised Frobenius F_K:K⊗^L_(A,σ)A→K of CR.3/frobenius-map, K=RΓ_crys(X/Spec A,E), becomes an isomorphism after inverting p. In particular, for a perfect field k of characteristic p, A=W(k) and σ the Witt vector Frobenius, the semilinear Frobenius of H^j_crys(X/W(k),E)[1/p] is bijective for every j. It need not be bijective on H^j_crys(X/W(k),E).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W_n=W_n(k), X a proper smooth k-scheme of pure dimension d, W_nX the scheme (|X|,W_nO_X) and f_n:W_nX→Spec W_n its structure map; f_n^! denotes the exceptional inverse image of coherent duality. (1) The complex f_n^!W_n is concentrated in degree −d, and there is a unique map of W_nO_X-modules Tr^Ek:W_nΩ^d_X→f_n^!W_n[−d] which, on every open U⊂X with a smooth lift U′ over W_n, is the composite of the isomorphism θ:W_nΩ^d_U≅σ^n_*H^d(Ω^•_(U′/W_n)) with the map induced by the coherent trace isomorphism Ω^d_(U′/W_n)≅f′^!W_n[−d] of f′:U′→Spec W_n. It is an isomorphism and is compatible with étale maps. (2) Through Ru_*O_crys≅W_nΩ^•_X (CR.4/crystalline-comparison), the isomorphism C^(−n):W_nΩ^d_X≅H^d(W_nΩ^•_X) and adjunction for the proper map f_n, it induces Tr^Ek_(X,n):RΓ_crys(X/W_n)→W_n[−2d], equivalently a W_n-linear map H^(2d)_crys(X/W_n)→W_n. These maps are compatible with reduction from W_n to W_(n−1), and Tr^Ek_(X,1):H^(2d)_dR(X/k)=H^d(X,Ω^d_X)→k is the trace of coherent duality. (3) Normalisation. For X=P^d, Tr^Ek_(X,n) sends to 1 the class [ω] of the Čech d-cocycle ω=dlog[t₁]∧…∧dlog[t_d] of the standard covering, [t_i]∈W_nO the Teichmüller representative of the coordinate t_i; and h^d=ε_d·[ω] in H^(2d)_crys(P^d/W_n) for a sign ε_d∈{1,−1} which depends only on d and on the sign conventions for products of Čech cochains. The crystalline trace is Tr_(X,n)=ε_d·Tr^Ek_(X,n), and Tr_X=Rlim_n Tr_(X,n):RΓ_crys(X/W)→W[−2d]; thus Tr_(P^d)(h^d)=1.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace_projective
missing.statement: Tr_(P^d)(h^d)=1 in W(k), for h=c₁(O(1)) and every d≥0; the same holds over W_n(k).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace_reduction
missing.statement: Tr_X⊗^L_W W_n=Tr_(X,n) under RΓ_crys(X/W)⊗^L_W W_n≅RΓ_crys(X/W_n), and Tr_(X,1):H^d(X,Ω^d_X)→k is ε_d times the trace of coherent duality.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace_etale_local
missing.statement: For an étale morphism g:U→X of smooth k-schemes of pure dimension d, g^*(Tr^Ek_X)=Tr^Ek_U under the identifications g^*W_nΩ^d_X≅W_nΩ^d_U and g^*f_(X,n)^!W_n≅f_(U,n)^!W_n (Ekedahl I, (2.11)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace_iso
missing.statement: Tr^Ek:W_nΩ^d_X→f_n^!W_n[−d] is an isomorphism of W_nO_X-modules, for X smooth of pure dimension d over k (Ekedahl I, Theorem 4.1).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace_ekedahl
missing.statement: Tr_(X,n)=ε_d·Tr^Ek_(X,n), where Tr^Ek is induced by Ekedahl's map (2.11), Tr^Ek_(P^d,n)([ω])=1 for the Čech class [ω] of dlog[t₁]∧…∧dlog[t_d], and ε_d∈{1,−1} is defined by h^d=ε_d·[ω].

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysTrace_frobenius
missing.statement: Tr_X(F(x))=p^d·σ(Tr_X(x)) for x∈H^(2d)_crys(X/W), F the semilinear Frobenius of CR.3/frobenius-map and σ the Frobenius of W(k); equivalently Tr_X is a map RΓ_crys(X/W)→W(−d)[−2d] compatible with Frobenius, W(−d) being W with Frobenius p^d·σ.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysTrace_point
missing.statement: For X=Spec k (d=0): Tr_X is the identity of W(k)=H⁰_crys(Spec k/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysTrace_P1
missing.statement: For P¹ over k: Tr(h)=1 for h=c₁(O(1))∈H²_crys(P¹/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysTrace_finite_extension
missing.statement: For X=Spec k′ with k′/k a finite extension (d=0): Tr_X:W(k′)→W(k) is the trace of the finite étale W(k)-algebra W(k′).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysPoincareDuality
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k), X a proper smooth k-scheme of pure dimension d and E a finite locally free crystal on X/W with dual E^∨; write K(E)=RΓ_crys(X/W,E). The pairing K(E)⊗^L_W K(E^∨)→K(E⊗E^∨)→K(O_crys)→W[−2d], composed of the cup product, the evaluation E⊗E^∨→O_crys and Tr_X, is perfect: its adjoint K(E)→RHom_W(K(E^∨),W)[−2d] is an isomorphism in D(W). The same holds over W_n(k) with Tr_(X,n), compatibly with ⊗^L_W W_n. For E=O_crys and H^i=H^i_crys(X/W): H^i[1/p]⊗H^(2d−i)[1/p]→W[1/p] is a perfect pairing of W[1/p]-vector spaces, (H^i/tors)⊗_W(H^(2d−i)/tors)→W is a perfect pairing, and H^i_tors≅Hom_W(H^(2d−i+1)_tors,W[1/p]/W).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysGysin
missing.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(k), and f:X→Y a morphism of proper smooth k-schemes of pure dimensions d_X and d_Y; write K(X)=RΓ_crys(X/W). (1) The Gysin map f_*:K(X)→K(Y)[2(d_Y−d_X)] is the transpose of f^*:K(Y)→K(X) under the duality isomorphisms of CR.3:duality/poincare-pairing: K(X)≅RHom_W(K(X),W)[−2d_X]→RHom_W(K(Y),W)[−2d_X]≅K(Y)[2(d_Y−d_X)]. missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.basicWittExpansion

A partition P of the support is a sequence of intervals I₀,…,I_q in increasing order, with I₀ allowed empty and the later intervals nonempty. Put t(I)=−min_(i∈I)v_p(k_i), u(I)=max(0,t(I)) and u(k)=max(0,−min_i v_p(k_i)); the weight k_I (the restriction of k to I) is integral when t(I)≤0, and the intervals with non-integral k_I come first. For ξ=V^u(k)(η) the basic form e(ξ,k,P) is the product, in order, of V^u(I₀)(η[T]^(p^u(I₀)k_I₀)) for block 0, dV^u(I)([T]^(p^u(I)k_I)) for each later block with k_I not integral, and F^(−t(I))d[T]^(p^t(I)k_I) for each later block with k_I integral. If I₀ is empty, η is placed inside the first factor, dV^u(I₁)(η[T]^(p^u(I₁)k_I₁)), when k is not integral, and in front of the product when k is integral. Every element of W_rΩ^q_(S/A) is uniquely a finite sum of basic forms e(ξ_(k,P),k,P) over weights with p^(r−1)·k integral (that is u(k)<r) and partitions into q+1 intervals, with ξ_(k,P)∈V^u(k)W_(r−u(k))(A). For an étale map R→S of F_p-algebras, W_r(WsatΩ_R)⊗_(W_r(R))W_r(S)≅W_r(WsatΩ_S) for every r. (4) For a scheme X over a Z_(p)-algebra A, U↦W_rΩ^q_(O(U)/A) on affine opens is a quasi-coherent sheaf on the scheme (|X|,W_r(O_X)), and an étale sheaf when p is nilpotent in A. For an F_p-scheme X, U↦W_r(WsatΩ^q_(O(U))) and U↦WsatΩ^q_(O(U)) are sheaves for the Zariski and the étale topology on affines, the former quasi-coherent over W_r(O_X), and the Zariski cohomology groups H^n(Spec R,WsatΩ^q) vanish for n>0.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.classicalSaturatedComparison
missing.statement: (1) Let R be a regular Noetherian F_p-algebra and {W_rΩ^*_R}_r its classical de Rham–Witt complex (CR.4/classical-de-rham-witt). The tower {W_r(WsatΩ_R)}_r, with its Verschiebung maps and the map W(R)→WsatΩ_R⁰ lifting e:R→S_R, is an R-framed V-pro-complex, and the resulting maps γ_r:W_rΩ^*_R→W_r(WsatΩ_R) are isomorphisms for all r≥0; hence γ:WΩ^*_R→WsatΩ_R is an isomorphism of differential graded algebras compatible with V, restriction and the maps from W(R), and ν:Ω^*_R→W_1(WsatΩ_R) is an isomorphism. Moreover the surjections W_rΩ^*_R→W_rΩ^*_(R/F_p) onto the Langer–Zink complex (CR.4/relative-de-rham-witt) are isomorphisms. (2) Let k be a perfect F_p-algebra and R a smooth k-algebra; then ν:Ω^*_R→W_1(WsatΩ_R) is an isomorphism. (3) Let B be a p-torsion-free ring with a ring endomorphism φ, φ(x)≡x^p mod p, such that B/pB is smooth over a perfect F_p-algebra. Then the p-completed de Rham complex Ω̂^*_B is a Dieudonné complex of Cartier type, and the map μ:Ω̂^*_B→WsatΩ_(B/pB) of CR.4/saturated-de-rham-witt is a quasi-isomorphism.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crystallineWittComparison
missing.statement: (a) Let A be a ring in which p is nilpotent and X a smooth A-scheme. For each r≥1 there is an isomorphism Ru_(r*)O_(X/W_r(A))≅W_rΩ^*_(X/A) in D⁺(X_Zar,W_r(A)), functorial in X, where u_r:(X/W_r(A))_crys→X_Zar and the crystalline site is formed with respect to the canonical divided powers on the kernel V W_(r−1)(A) of the projection w₀:W_r(A)→A. (b) More generally, for a quasi-coherent crystal E of flat modules on (X/W_r(A))_crys, Ru_(r*)E is represented by E_r⊗_(W_r(O_X))W_rΩ^*_(X/A), where E_r is the value of E on the PD thickening X→W_r(X) and the differential is induced by the connection of the crystal. (c) For X smooth over a perfect field k (the case A=k), these isomorphisms are compatible in r and give Ru_*O_(X/W(k))≅Rlim_r W_rΩ^*_(X/k)≅WΩ^*_(X/k), and the corresponding isomorphisms on RΓ(X,−); here lim_r W_rΩ^q=Rlim_r W_rΩ^q because the restriction maps are surjective on affine opens.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.wittCrystallineFrobenius
missing.statement: In every F–V procomplex dF=pFd, so the graded Frobenius F is in general not a map of complexes. Let p be nilpotent in A and X a smooth A-scheme. The absolute Frobenius 𝐅:W_rΩ^q_(X/A)→W_(r−1)Ω^q_(X/A), 𝐅=p^q·F, is a map of complexes, semilinear over F:W_r(A)→W_(r−1)(A); it is the map induced on de Rham–Witt complexes by F:W_r(O_X)→W_(r−1)(O_X). The crystalline complexes carry an absolute Frobenius 𝐅:Ru_(r*)O_(X/W_r(A))→Ru_((r−1)*)O_(X/W_(r−1)(A)), induced by the absolute Frobenius of X₀=X⊗F_p and the PD morphism Spec W_(r−1)(A)→Spec W_r(A) given by F, for the divided powers extended to the kernel of W_r(A)→A/pA. The comparison isomorphisms of CR.4/crystalline-comparison at levels r and r−1 intertwine the two maps 𝐅. For X smooth over a perfect field k, the limit over r is the endomorphism φ=p^q·F of the complex WΩ^*_(X/k), and it corresponds to the crystalline Frobenius of Ru_*O_(X/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.strictDieudonneFixedPoint
missing.statement: Let D(Z)^_p be the full subcategory of derived p-complete objects of D(Z); Lη_p preserves it. Sending a strict Dieudonné complex M to the pair (M,α_F:M≅Lη_pM) is an equivalence from the category of strict Dieudonné complexes to the fixed-point category of Lη_p on D(Z)^_p, whose objects are pairs (X,φ:X≅Lη_pX) and whose morphisms are the maps X→X′ in D(Z) commuting with φ, φ′. The fixed-point ∞-category, defined as the equalizer of the identity and Lη_p on the ∞-category of derived p-complete objects of the derived ∞-category of Z (so that objects carry a specified equivalence and morphisms a specified homotopy), has discrete mapping spaces, and the forgetful functor from it to the ordinary fixed-point category is an equivalence. For strict M, F^r induces isomorphisms W_r(M)≅H^*(M/p^rM), so M=lim_r W_r(M) is recovered from the cohomology of the reductions M⊗^L Z/p^r.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.wittSlopeSpectralSequence
missing.statement: Let X be a smooth proper scheme of dimension d over a perfect field k, W=W(k), K=W[1/p]. The filtration of WΩ^*_X by the subcomplexes WΩ^(≥a)_X, 0≤a≤d, gives a convergent spectral sequence E₁^(a,b)=H^b(X,WΩ^a_X)⇒H^(a+b)_crys(X/W), compatible with the Frobenius φ, which acts on the a-th column through p^a·F. After tensoring with K, the E₁ terms are finite-dimensional over K, the Frobenius on the a-th column has slopes in [a,a+1), and the spectral sequence degenerates at E₁; so H^b(X,WΩ^a_X)⊗K is the part of H^(a+b)_crys(X/W)⊗K with slopes in [a,a+1). For each r≥1 the same filtration of W_rΩ^*_X gives a spectral sequence E₁^(a,b)=H^b(X,W_rΩ^a_X)⇒H^(a+b)_crys(X/W_r(k)).

(1) The composite N^(≥i)WΩ--φ_i→WΩ→Ω^*_(R/k) lands in the canonical truncation τ^(≤i)Ω^*_(R/k), kills N^(≥i+1)WΩ, and induces a quasi-isomorphism gr^i_N WΩ→τ^(≤i)Ω^*_(R/k). (2) The sequence WΩ/N^(≥i)--p→WΩ/N^(≥i+1)→Ω^(≤i)_(R/k) is a cofiber sequence, where Ω^(≤i) is the stupid truncation and the second map is induced by WΩ→Ω^*_(R/k)→Ω^(≤i)_(R/k). (3) Let Ã be the p-adic completion of a smooth W(k)-algebra lifting R, with a chosen lift φ̃ of Frobenius, and let σ:Ω̂^*_(Ã/W(k))→WΩ be the comparison map constructed from φ̃. Then σ maps the subcomplex p^max(i−•,0)Ω̂^•_(Ã/W(k)), with terms p^(i−q)Ω̂^q for q<i and Ω̂^q for q≥i, into N^(≥i)WΩ, and the induced map is a quasi-isomorphism for every i≥0.
