missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.logWittExactSequences
missing.statement: Let X be a regular locally Noetherian F_p-scheme and q≥0; all sheaves are on the small étale site of X. (1) For r≥1, F:W_(r+1)Ω^q_X→W_rΩ^q_X induces F:W_rΩ^q_X→W_rΩ^q_X/dV^(r−1)Ω^(q−1)_X (with Ω^(−1)=0), and the sequence 0→W_rΩ^q_(X,log)→W_rΩ^q_X--1−F→W_rΩ^q_X/dV^(r−1)Ω^(q−1)_X→0 is exact. (2) The sequence of pro-sheaves 0→W_•Ω^q_(X,log)→W_•Ω^q_X--R−F→W_•Ω^q_X→0 is exact. (3) For positive integers n, m, multiplication by p^m on W_(n+m)Ω^q_(X,log) induces a map p̲^m:W_nΩ^q_(X,log)→W_(n+m)Ω^q_(X,log), and the sequence 0→W_nΩ^q_(X,log)--p̲^m→W_(n+m)Ω^q_(X,log)--R^n→W_mΩ^q_(X,log)→0 is exact; consequently 0→W_•Ω^q_(X,log)--p^m→W_•Ω^q_(X,log)→W_mΩ^q_(X,log)→0 is an exact sequence of pro-sheaves.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittModel
missing.statement: Let κ be a perfect field of characteristic p, W=W(κ), K₀=W[1/p]. Let W[t]° be Spec W[t] with the log structure associated with 1↦t, W° its fibre at t=0, κ° the fibre of W° at p=0 (the standard log point), and W^triv=Spec W with the trivial log structure. Let (X,L) be a log scheme of finite type and strictly semistable over κ°, and {(X^⋆,L^⋆)↪(Z^⋆,N^⋆)} an admissible embedding system for (X,L)/W[t]°; put (Y^⋆,M^⋆)=(Z^⋆,N^⋆)×_(W[t]°)W°, and for l≥1 let D_l^⋆ be the PD envelope of X^⋆ in Y_l^⋆=Y^⋆⊗Z/p^l, over W with its usual divided powers. Define, in D⁺(X_ét,W_•) (systems indexed by l), Wω_X=Ru_*(Ω^*_((Y^⋆,M^⋆)/W°)⊗O_(D_l^⋆)) and Wω̃_X=Ru_*(Ω^*_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)⊗O_(D_l^⋆)), where u:X^⋆→X is the augmentation of the hypercovering. They do not depend on the embedding system. After applying Rlim_l and ⊗_W K₀ there is a distinguished triangle Wω_(X,K₀)[−1]→Wω̃_(X,K₀)→Wω_(X,K₀)--N→Wω_(X,K₀) in D⁺(X_ét,K₀), whose first map is ∧dlog t, whose second map is the natural projection, and whose third map N is the connecting map. The convergent complexes ω_X, ω̃_X∈D⁺(X_ét,K₀) of Disegni–Liu (the same differential forms with the tube of X^⋆ in place of the PD envelopes) are related to them by natural equivalences ω_X≃Wω_(X,K₀), ω̃_X≃Wω̃_(X,K₀), under which the triangle (B.1) of Disegni–Liu corresponds to this one.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittModel.envelope_eval
missing.statement: For an admissible embedding system, Wω_X and Wω̃_X are represented by Ru_* of the complexes Ω^*_((Y^⋆,M^⋆)/W°)⊗O_(D_l^⋆) and Ω^*_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)⊗O_(D_l^⋆), l≥1, on the hypercovering X^⋆.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittModel.embedding_independence
missing.statement: The product-embedding maps are compatible quasi-isomorphisms and satisfy the cocycle.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittModel.rational_compare
missing.statement: There are natural equivalences ω_X≃Wω_(X,K₀) and ω̃_X≃Wω̃_(X,K₀) in D⁺(X_ét,K₀) (Disegni–Liu (B.5)) carrying the triangle (B.1) of the convergent complexes to the triangle (B.4); in particular they commute with the maps ∧dlog t.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittModel.monodromy_triangle
missing.statement: Wω_(X,K₀)[−1]--∧dlog t→Wω̃_(X,K₀)→Wω_(X,K₀)--N→Wω_(X,K₀) is a distinguished triangle in D⁺(X_ét,K₀), and N is its connecting map (Disegni–Liu (B.4)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_logWittModel_point
missing.statement: For X=κ° with the embedding κ°↪W[t]° (Z=Spec W[t], Y=W°, D_l=Spec W/p^l): Wω_X=(W/p^l)_l in degree 0, Wω̃_X=(W/p^l⊕W/p^l·dlog t)_l in degrees 0 and 1 with zero differential, and the connecting map N of the triangle is 0.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_logWittModel_diagonal_embedding
missing.statement: For an admissible embedding system E of (X,L), the isomorphisms Wω_X(E)≅Wω_X(E) and Wω̃_X(E)≅Wω̃_X(E) obtained by comparing E with itself through the product system E×E and its two projections are the identity maps.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_logWittModel_rational_scope
missing.statement: For X=κ° with the embedding κ°↪W[t]°: the tube of X in the generic fibre of the formal completion of Y=W° is the point Sp K₀, so ω_X=K₀ in degree 0 and ω̃_X=K₀⊕K₀·dlog t in degrees 0 and 1 with zero differential; Wω_(X,K₀) and Wω̃_(X,K₀) are the same complexes, and the equivalences of (B.5) are the identity maps.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittSupport
missing.statement: In the situation of CR.4/semistable-log-witt-models let F:U→X be the inclusion of an open subscheme, and let ω̃_(U,X), ω⁺_(U,X)∈D⁺(X_ét,K₀) be the convergent complexes with support of Disegni–Liu, defined like ω̃_X and ω⁺_X with the tube functor f^!_(U^⋆,X^⋆) inserted (f^! is the kernel of the unit id→g_*g^* for the open immersion g of the tube of X^⋆∖U^⋆ into the tube of X^⋆). (1) There is a natural map F_!F^*Wω̃_(X,K₀)→ω̃_(U,X) in D⁺(X_ét,K₀) (Disegni–Liu (B.6)): F_!F^* applied to the inverse of the equivalence ω̃_X≃Wω̃_(X,K₀), followed by the natural transformation F_!∘F^*∘Rs_*→Rs_*∘f^! of their Lemma B.3. (2) Let WΞ_X∈D⁺(X_ét,W_•) be Sato's cohomological de Rham–Witt complex, with the equivalence ω⁺_X≃WΞ_(X,K₀). In the same way there is a natural map F_!F^*WΞ_(X,K₀)→ω⁺_(U,X) (Disegni–Liu (B.9)). (3) These two maps form a commutative square (Disegni–Liu (B.10)) with the map F_!F^*Wω̃_(X,K₀)→F_!F^*WΞ_(X,K₀)[−1] induced by Sato's map Wω̃_X→WΞ_X[−1] and the map ω̃_(U,X)→ω⁺_(U,X)[−1] induced by the quotient maps Ω^(q+1)_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)⊗O_(Y^⋆)→Ξ^q_(Z^⋆)=Ω^(q+1)_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)/Ω^(q+1)_(Z^⋆/W). The map ∧dlog t is the map ω_(U,X)[−1]→ω̃_(U,X) of Disegni–Liu (B.8); it does not occur in (B.10). For U=X the tube functor is the identity and the maps (1), (2) are the inverses of the comparison equivalences.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittSupport.compare
missing.statement: Natural maps F_!F^*Wω̃_(X,K₀)→ω̃_(U,X) and F_!F^*WΞ_(X,K₀)→ω⁺_(U,X) in D⁺(X_ét,K₀) (Disegni–Liu (B.6), (B.9)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittSupport.open_identity
missing.statement: For U=X, the tube support functor is the identity and the comparison recovers the full rational model comparison.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.LogWittSupport.dlog_square
missing.statement: The maps (B.6) and (B.9) form a commutative square with F_!F^*Wω̃_(X,K₀)→F_!F^*WΞ_(X,K₀)[−1], induced by Sato's map, and ω̃_(U,X)→ω⁺_(U,X)[−1], induced by the quotient maps Ω^(q+1)_((Z^⋆,N^⋆)/W^triv)⊗O_(Y^⋆)→Ξ^q_(Z^⋆) (Disegni–Liu (B.10)). The map ∧dlog t is not an arrow of this square.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_logWittSupport_empty
missing.statement: For U=∅: g is the identity of the tube of X^⋆, f^!_(∅,X)=ker(id→id)=0, so ω̃_(∅,X)=ω⁺_(∅,X)=0, and the sources F_!F^*(−) of (B.6) and (B.9) are 0.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_logWittSupport_full
missing.statement: For U=X: the tube of X∖U is empty, f^!_(X,X) is the identity, ω̃_(X,X)=ω̃_X, and (B.6) is the inverse of the equivalence ω̃_X≃Wω̃_(X,K₀) of (B.5).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_logWittSupport_map
missing.statement: The natural transformation F_!∘F^*∘Rs_*→Rs_*∘f^!_(U,X) of Disegni–Liu Lemma B.3 is not an isomorphism of functors in general, even when X=Z: otherwise f=F_!∘F^* would satisfy f∘Rs_*≃Rs_*∘f^!_(U,X), and by their Remark B.2 no functor f on D⁺(X_ét,R) does in general.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crisDifferentials
missing.statement: On Cris(X/S), Ω_{X/S} with d_{X/S}:O_crys→Ω_{X/S} is the universal PD S-derivation; (Ω_{X/S})_T=Ω_{T/S,δ} and d_{X/S} restricts to d_{T/S,δ}; Ω_{X/S} has quasi-coherent restrictions and c_f:f^*(Ω_{X/S})_T′→(Ω_{X/S})_T is surjective when f:T→T′ is a closed immersion, but Ω_{X/S} is in general not a crystal (Stacks Lemmas 60.12.3 and 60.12.6).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.Connection.ofCrystal
missing.statement: A crystal F in O_crys-modules on Cris(X/S) carries a canonical integrable connection: for an object (U,T,δ), with T′ the first-order thickening O_T′=O_T⊕Ω_{T/S,δ}, projections p₀,p₁:T′→T and c=c_{p₁}⁻¹∘c_{p₀}:p₀^*F_T→p₁^*F_T, one has ∇(s)=p₁^*s−c(p₀^*s) in F_T⊗_{O_T}Ω_{T/S,δ} (Stacks Lemma 60.15.1).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern
missing.statement: Let (S,I,γ) be a PD scheme over Z_(p), S₀=V(I), and X an S₀-scheme on which p is locally nilpotent. On the crystalline site of X/S let O_crys, O_X^cris and J_crys=ker(O_crys→O_X^cris) be the sheaves of CR.1/structure-sheaves, δ the divided powers of J_crys, and u:(X/S)_crys→X_Zar the projection. (1) The sequence of sheaves of abelian groups 1→1+J_crys→O_crys^*→(O_X^cris)^*→1 is exact, and (O_X^cris)^*=u^(−1)O_X^*. (2) log:1+J_crys→J_crys, log(1+x)=Σ_(n≥1)(−1)^(n−1)·(n−1)!·δ_n(x), is a homomorphism from the multiplicative group 1+J_crys to the additive group J_crys; on each thickening the sum is locally finite because p is locally nilpotent there. (3) The first Chern class c₁:Pic(X)=H¹(X,O_X^*)→H²_crys(X/S)=H²((X/S)_crys,O_crys) is the composite of u^(−1), the connecting homomorphism H¹((O_X^cris)^*)→H²(1+J_crys) of (1), the map induced by log, and the map induced by J_crys⊂O_crys. (4) The sign of the connecting homomorphism is fixed by the following property: if p is nilpotent on S, Y is a smooth lift of X over S and L̃ is an invertible O_Y-module lifting L, with trivialising sections s_λ on an open cover, then under H²_crys(X/S)≅H²(Y,Ω^•_(Y/S)) the class c₁(L) is the class of the Čech 1-cocycle (dlog(s_μ/s_λ))_(λ,μ) with values in Ω¹_(Y/S), the de Rham first Chern class of L̃. (5) c₁ is a homomorphism of groups and is natural for the morphisms of crystalline topoi induced by commutative squares of schemes over PD morphisms. (6) For a perfect field k of characteristic p and X proper smooth over k, c₁(L)∈H²_crys(X/W(k)) is the compatible system of the classes c₁(L)∈H²_crys(X/W_n(k)); the hyperplane class is h=c₁(O(1))∈H²_crys(P^d_k/W(k)).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_log
missing.statement: log((1+x)(1+y))=log(1+x)+log(1+y) for local sections x, y of J_crys, where log(1+x)=Σ_(n≥1)(−1)^(n−1)·(n−1)!·δ_n(x).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_add
missing.statement: c₁(L⊗M)=c₁(L)+c₁(M), c₁(O_X)=0 and c₁(L^∨)=−c₁(L) for invertible O_X-modules L, M.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_pullback
missing.statement: For a morphism g:X′→X over a morphism of PD schemes S′→S: g^*c₁(L)=c₁(g^*L) in H²_crys(X′/S′).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_fil
missing.statement: c₁(L) lies in the image of H²((X/S)_crys,J_crys)→H²_crys(X/S).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_deRham
missing.statement: If p is locally nilpotent on S, Y is a smooth lift of X over S and L̃ an invertible O_Y-module lifting L with trivialising sections s_λ, then under H²_crys(X/S)≅H²(Y,Ω^•_(Y/S)) of CR.2/smooth-lift-filtration c₁(L) is the class of the Čech 1-cocycle (dlog(s_μ/s_λ)) with values in Ω¹_(Y/S).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_reduction
missing.statement: For k perfect and X proper smooth over k, the reduction H²_crys(X/W(k))→H²_crys(X/W_n(k)) sends c₁(L) to c₁(L), and for n=1 the image is the de Rham class c₁^dR(L)∈H²_dR(X/k).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.crysChern_hyperplane
missing.statement: h=c₁(O(1))∈H²_crys(P^d_k/W(k)) for a perfect field k of characteristic p and d≥1.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysChern_P1
missing.statement: For a perfect field k of characteristic p, H²_crys(P¹_k/W_n(k)) is free of rank one over W_n(k) with basis h=c₁(O(1)); under H²_crys(P¹_k/W_n)≅H²(P¹_(W_n),Ω^•) the class h is that of the Čech 1-cocycle dt/t on U₀∩U₁, t=T₁/T₀.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysChern_twist
missing.statement: c₁(O(m))=m·h in H²_crys(P^d_k/W(k)) for every integer m.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysChern_mod_p
missing.statement: For k a perfect field of characteristic p and S=Spec k: c₁(O(p))=0 in H²_crys(P¹_k/k)=H²_dR(P¹_k/k), although O(p) is not trivial and c₁(O(p))=p·h≠0 in H²_crys(P¹_k/W(k)); so c₁ is not injective, and the class over W(k) is not determined by its reduction modulo p.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_crysChern_trivial
missing.statement: c₁(O_X)=0 in H²_crys(X/S).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower
missing.statement: A strict Dieudonné tower is an inverse system ⋯→X_3→X_2→X_1→X_0 of cochain complexes of abelian groups, with transition maps R:X_(r+1)→X_r, equipped with maps of graded abelian groups F:X_(r+1)→X_r and V:X_r→X_(r+1) for every r≥0, such that: (1) X_0=0; (2) R:X_(r+1)→X_r is surjective for every r≥0; (3) F:X_(r+1)→X_r satisfies dF=pFd for every r≥0; (4) F, R and V commute with each other; (5) F(V(x))=p·x=V(F(x)) for every x∈X_r; (6) every x∈X_r such that dx is divisible by p lies in the image of F:X_(r+1)→X_r; (7) the kernel of R:X_(r+1)→X_r is the subgroup X_(r+1)[p] of elements x with p·x=0; (8) the kernel of R:X_(r+1)→X_r is the span of the images of V^r:X_1→X_(r+1) and dV^r:X_1→X_(r+1). A morphism of strict Dieudonné towers is a morphism of towers of cochain complexes compatible with F and V; TD denotes the category of strict Dieudonné towers. (a) For a saturated Dieudonné complex M, the tower (W_r(M))_(r≥0) with the maps Res, F and V of CR.4/verschiebung-completion-tower is a strict Dieudonné tower. (b) For a strict Dieudonné tower (X_r), the inverse limit X=lim_r X_r, with F the inverse limit of the maps F:X_(r+1)→X_r, is a saturated Dieudonné complex; for every r≥0 the projection X→X_r induces an isomorphism of cochain complexes W_r(X)=X/(im V^r+im dV^r)≅X_r; these isomorphisms form an isomorphism of strict Dieudonné towers (W_r(X))_r≅(X_r)_r; and X is a strict Dieudonné complex. (c) The functor M↦(W_r(M))_(r≥0) from the category DC_str of strict Dieudonné complexes to TD is an equivalence of categories, with inverse (X_r)_(r≥0)↦lim_r X_r.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.ofSaturated
missing.statement: For a saturated Dieudonné complex M, the complexes W_r(M) (r≥0) with Res:W_(r+1)(M)→W_r(M), F:W_(r+1)(M)→W_r(M) and V:W_r(M)→W_(r+1)(M) form a strict Dieudonné tower (BLM Proposition 2.6.2).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.limit
missing.statement: For a strict Dieudonné tower X, the inverse limit lim_r X_r with (Fx)_r=F(x_(r+1)) is a saturated Dieudonné complex, and its Verschiebung is given by (Vx)_(r+1)=V(x_r), (Vx)_0=0 (BLM Proposition 2.6.5).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.limitWIso
missing.statement: For a strict Dieudonné tower X and every r≥0, the projection lim_s X_s→X_r is surjective with kernel im V^r+im dV^r; so it induces an isomorphism of cochain complexes W_r(lim_s X_s)≅X_r, and these isomorphisms commute with R, F and V (BLM Proposition 2.9.1, Corollary 2.9.2).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.limit_isStrict
missing.statement: For a strict Dieudonné tower X, lim_r X_r is a strict Dieudonné complex in the sense of CR.4/strict-dieudonne-complex (BLM Corollary 2.9.3).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.Hom
missing.statement: A morphism X→Y of strict Dieudonné towers is a family of maps of cochain complexes f_r:X_r→Y_r with R∘f_(r+1)=f_r∘R, F∘f_(r+1)=f_r∘F and V∘f_r=f_(r+1)∘V. It induces a morphism of Dieudonné complexes lim f:lim_r X_r→lim_r Y_r, with lim(id)=id and lim(g∘f)=lim(g)∘lim(f); a morphism f:M→N of saturated Dieudonné complexes induces the morphism (W_r(f))_r of towers, compatibly with identities and composition.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.equivalence
missing.statement: M↦(W_r(M))_r, from strict Dieudonné complexes to strict Dieudonné towers, and X↦lim_r X_r are inverse equivalences of categories: ρ_M:M→lim_r W_r(M) is a natural isomorphism for strict M, and W_r(lim_s X_s)≅X_r is a natural isomorphism of towers (BLM Corollary 2.9.4).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.StrictDieudonneTower.relations
missing.statement: In a strict Dieudonné tower: p^r·X_r=0 for every r≥0 (by (1) and (7), by induction on r); and V∘d=p·d∘V:X_r^n→X_(r+1)^(n+1) and F∘d∘V=d:X_r^n→X_r^(n+1). The last two are not axioms; they follow from X_r≅W_r(lim X) and the identities Vd=p·dV, FdV=d on the saturated complex lim X.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_tower_Zp
missing.statement: The tower of Z_p (degree 0, F=id) is X_r=Z/p^r with R and F the projections Z/p^(r+1)→Z/p^r and V multiplication by p, Z/p^r→Z/p^(r+1). It satisfies the eight axioms: ker(R:X_(r+1)→X_r)=p^r·Z/p^(r+1)=X_(r+1)[p]=V^r(X_1), and F is surjective. Its limit is Z_p with F=id and V=p.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_tower_constant_Fp
missing.statement: Let X_0=0 and X_r=F_p in degree 0 for r≥1, with R:X_(r+1)→X_r and F:X_(r+1)→X_r the identity for r≥1 and zero for r=0, and V=0. Axioms (1)–(6) and (8) hold, and (7) fails: for r≥1, ker(R:X_(r+1)→X_r)=0 and X_(r+1)[p]=F_p. The limit F_p is not p-torsion-free.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_tower_rational
missing.statement: The zero tower (X_r=0 for all r) is a strict Dieudonné tower with limit 0. It is the tower of the saturated complex Q (degree 0, F=id), for which V=p is bijective and W_r(Q)=0; so lim_r W_r(M)≅M fails for the non-strict saturated complex M=Q.

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_tower_localization
missing.statement: The saturated complexes Z_(p) and Z_p (degree 0, F=id) have the same tower (Z/p^r)_r, and its limit Z_p is the completion W(Z_(p)) of CR.4/verschiebung-completion-tower; for a saturated M, lim_r of the tower (W_r(M))_r is W(M).

missing.name: TauCeti.Crystalline.test_tower_free
missing.statement: Let X_r⁰=⊕_(m≥0)(Z/p^r)·e_m ⊕ ⊕_(0<n<r)(Z/p^(r−n))·v_n and X_r¹=⊕_(m≥0)(Z/p^r)·f_m ⊕ ⊕_(0<n<r)(Z/p^(r−n))·w_n, with d(e_m)=p^m·f_m, d(v_n)=w_n, R the projections, F(e_m)=e_(m+1), F(v_n)=p·v_(n−1), F(f_m)=f_(m+1), F(w_n)=w_(n−1), V(e_m)=p·e_(m−1) for m≥1, V(e_0)=v_1, V(v_n)=v_(n+1), V(f_m)=p·f_(m−1) for m≥1, V(f_0)=p·w_1, V(w_n)=p·w_(n+1), where v_0=e_0 and w_0=f_0. This is a strict Dieudonné tower with nonzero differential (d(e_0)=f_0 in X_1); it is the tower of the free strict Dieudonné complex on x=e_0 of BLM Example 2.5.7, with e_m=F^m x, v_n=V^n x, f_m=F^m dx, w_n=dV^n x.

restructure.detail: Ordinary differential forms with their exterior derivative, wedge product and universal property are owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2 (nodes DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex, DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-universal-property, DD.2/formal-ordinary-derham), not by DD.0, whose description is cotangent complexes and derived powers. After the corrections no node of the packet cites DD.0. DD.2 requires only DD.0 and DD.1 and has no path to CrystallineCohomology:CR.1, CR.2 or CR.4 in the stage graph (stageEdges plus requires, computed by findings/G7/graph.py), so moving CR.1/pd-differentials and CR.1/envelope-differentials to CR.1 creates no cycle: their external suppliers are then DD.2 nodes and mathlib:AdicCompletion, and their packet prerequisites are in CR.0.

restructure.detail: CR.4/semistable-log-witt-models and CR.4/log-witt-proper-support need the convergent side of Disegni–Liu Appendix B: tubes of an embedding system of a strictly semistable log scheme with quasi-étale sites, specialization to the étale site, the functor f^!_{(U,X)} and the complexes ω, ω̃, ω⁺. restructure.proposal: Either add a log-rigid stage to PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology (log tubes, specialization, convergent log de Rham complexes of semistable log schemes, after RD.3/RD.4 and CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra) and link it to CR.4, or move the two nodes out of CR.4 into CrystallineCohomology:CR.6, whose description already has "Develop the log de Rham–Witt or embedding-system model needed for this proof"; they are not among the targets CR.4's description states. Until then the need is a gap.

restructure.detail: The acceptance example of CR.3 "an elliptic curve in each ordinary/supersingular case" was to be proved through the comparison H¹_crys(E/W)≅M(E[p^∞]), requested from R07.2. R07.2 requires CR.0 and CR.1 only; the comparison needs RΓ_crys, its finiteness and its Frobenius (CR.2, CR.3), so supplying it from R07.2 to CR.3 is a cycle. No node of any packet states the comparison.
restructure.proposal: Own the comparison H¹_crys(A/W(k))≅M(A[p^∞]) (elliptic curves first, abelian schemes if wanted) in CrystallineCohomology:CR.7, adding CR.3 to CR.7's prerequisites (CR.7 already requires R07.2; CR.3 does not depend on CR.7), or in a FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory stage that may require CR.3. Move the elliptic slope acceptance from CR.3 to that stage, or prove it in CR.3 without Dieudonné theory. This supersedes the packet's earlier proposal "extend R07.2 with elliptic crystalline realization".

restructure.detail: Coherent cohomology of proper flat morphisms is planned in three places: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension by description ("Extend proper-flat coherent cohomology and base change beyond curves"), with no node yet; SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.2 by nodes (proper-perfect-pushforward-perfect, derived-tor-independent-base-change, derived-projection-formula, with Grothendieck's coherence theorem recorded there as a gap); SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 by promoted nodes for coherent duality. restructure.proposal: Decide one owner for finiteness, perfectness, base change, cohomological amplitude and Künneth of coherent cohomology (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 is the most foundational of the three) and have the other two import it; state the coherent Künneth formula and the bound R^if_*F=0 for i>d there.

restructure.detail: Dieudonné–Manin and slope decompositions are stated at three generalities: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0 over the completed maximal unramified extension of a local field (residue field an algebraic closure of F_q); PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical over any algebraically closed residue field; PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/slope-decomposition over W(k)[1/p] for k perfect. restructure.proposal: Record RD.1 as the owner of Dieudonné–Manin over a general algebraically closed residue field and R06.2 as the owner of the descent to perfect fields, with VB0 the F̄_q case; repoint R07.2/dieudonne-slopes to RD.1/dieudonne-manin-classical or R06.2/slope-decomposition.

restructure.detail: PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/restriction-to-convergent requests from CrystallineCohomology:CR.3 the category F-Isoc(X/K) of convergent F-isocrystals (coherent modules on tubes with convergent Taylor isomorphism and a Frobenius; independence of the embedding; tensor structure; comparison with F-crystals up to isogeny, Ogus). The promoted SchemeAndStackFoundations packet plans coherent duality under SF.2 (node SchemeAndStackFoundations:key/coherent-duality, with SF.2/serre-proper, SF.2/smooth-proper and SF.2/trace), although the description of SF.2 in data/atlas.json does not mention it and the register data/keydefs lists no owner for the key definition algebraicgeometry/coherent-duality. restructure.proposal: Add to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (or to the single owner of proper coherent cohomology chosen under the merge proposal of the earlier pass) three nodes: the smooth and étale shriek formulas without properness; Hodge cohomology of projective space with the class of O(1); and the vanishing of the coherent trace on d(H^d(X,Ω^{d−1})). sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts the existence of a triangle with a third member whose cohomology is killed by $p$. It invokes TR4 in the triangulated category $D(X)$ without supplying details.
sourceIssues.correction: The proof concludes 'Thus we see that the result follows from this lemma', i.e. from Lemma 60.25.3, which states only that there is a map e with c∘e and e∘c homotopic to multiplication by p. That property gives a cone whose cohomology is annihilated by p², not by p. What gives p is in the proof of Lemma 60.25.1: c is termwise injective, e∘c = a exactly, and the homotopy h vanishes on the image of c (h(fω)=0), so h induces d∘h+h∘d = a on the cokernel of c, which is quasi-isomorphic to the cone.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample to the formal implication: K=[Z→Z] (multiplication by p) in degrees 0,1, L=[Z→Z] (multiplication by p) in degrees −1,0, c the identity K⁰→L⁰ and e=0. Then c∘e and e∘c are homotopic to p, and the cone of c has H⁰=Z/p². The statement of Lemma 60.25.4 is correct; the deduction needs the finer properties of e and h.

sourceIssues.locator: §5.5, proof of Theorem 5.3.4, pp.66–67 of arXiv v3 (the same in Astérisque 424, p.68); the same point in the proof of Proposition 5.5.1, p.65 ('Invoking Proposition 5.3.2 again')
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts unique extensions of the restriction and Frobenius maps R,F∶Wn(S) → Wn−1(S) to commutative differential graded algebra maps R,F∶B∗ n → B∗ n−1.
sourceIssues.correction: R extends uniquely to a map of commutative differential graded algebras; F extends uniquely to a map of graded rings F:B^*_n→B^*_(n−1) compatible with F on 𝒲_n(A)^*, and it satisfies dF=pFd. Proposition 5.3.2(2) gives this when B^*_n and 𝒲_n(A)^* carry the differential p·d, for which F:𝒲_n(A)^*→𝒲_(n−1)(A)^* is a map of differential graded algebras.
sourceIssues.reason: F:𝒲_n(A)^*→𝒲_(n−1)(A)^* satisfies dF=pFd and is not a map of differential graded algebras, so B^*_(n−1) is not a 𝒲_n(A)^*-algebra through F in the sense of §5.3 and Proposition 5.3.2(2) does not apply as cited. If the extension commuted with d, then F(dx)=0 in 𝒲_(n−1)(A)¹ for all x∈𝒲_n(A)⁰, whereas F(d[T])=[T]^(p−1)d[T]≠0 for A=𝒲Ω_(F_p[T]) and n≥2. The proof itself goes on to treat F as 'a map of graded algebras' and leaves dF=pFd (axiom (3) of Definition 2.6.1) to the reader. With the differential p·d on the source the cited proposition applies, in both proofs, and yields dF=pFd.

review.notes: Independent review of all 150 nodes against the sources at the pinned versions, of the 91 baseline declarations at the pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti commits, of the 18 source issues at their locators, of every cross-roadmap prerequisite against the supplier node or stage, and of the suggested Lean file. The packet was corrected in place. Corrections of substance: the sign of the Taylor isomorphism (CR.1/taylor-equivalence); the target of Ru_* (D(X_Zar,f⁻¹O_S), not D(O_X)); a false universal property of the completed envelope; a false test of the linearization; the hypothesis of geometric connectedness for curves; the classical/saturated comparison, which BLM prove for regular Noetherian F_p-algebras; the diagram (B.10) of Disegni–Liu; a prerequisite on AInfCohomology:AI.0 that closed a stage cycle (replaced by Mathlib's fontaineTheta). Placeholder excerpts, boilerplate acceptance items and process remarks in node fields were replaced throughout; locators were checked against the tags file of the pinned Stacks commit. Fourteen nodes were added, two nodes moved from CR.2 to CR.1, the baseline grew from 91 to 153 declarations (one removed), the requests were rewritten as exact statements, the gaps were rebuilt from what the sources leave unproved, and 48 source issues were added. A second reading of all nodes by readers who had not seen the findings was applied. Illusie's 1979 paper, recorded as not acquired, was obtained and the nodes resting on it were checked. Status needs_changes: the reader document of the roadmap part was written for the uncorrected packet and now contradicts it (the review may not edit it); three stages are marked partial with precise remaining lists; details and the tasks of the revision are in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-CrystallineCohomology--CR.0.md.
